checklist.step: Open the annual cycle and lock the Section 802 deliverable list
actions: Re-read PMIERs Section 802 and both Enterprises' current Approved Insurer reporting instructions and list every annual deliverable: audited consolidated GAAP financial statements (non-public entity), the annual convention statement as filed with state insurance regulators, and the related regulator correspondence.
Ask each Enterprise's Approved Insurer relationship manager, in writing, to confirm the delivery channel and file naming for the reporting year, and file the reply.

Build the cycle plan with the fixed dates: trial balance certified January 31, blank draft February 15, NAIC filing March 1, audited GAAP statements April 1, CFO signature April 8, Enterprise delivery April 15.
Name an owner for each deliverable (Controller, Reserving Actuary, Appointed Actuary, Regulatory Reporting Manager) and publish the plan to the close workspace.
checklist.done: the deliverable list, per-Enterprise delivery channel and dated owner plan are published and confirmed in writing by both Enterprises.

checklist.step: Close the December ledger and certify the statutory trial balance
actions: Run the December 31 hard close in the general ledger for the mortgage guaranty writing company and confirm all sub-ledgers (premium, loss, reinsurance ceded, investment) are posted and the period is locked.
Export the statutory-basis trial balance by NAIC line of business and reconcile total assets, liabilities and surplus to the close/consolidation tool balance sheet.
Clear every open close reconciliation item above the $50,000 posting threshold with Senior Accountant support, and document any item passed as immaterial.
Sign the trial balance certification and hand the locked extract to the Statutory Reporting Manager.
checklist.done: the December 31 trial balance is locked, reconciled to the consolidation balance sheet and certified in writing by the Controller.

checklist.step: Map the trial balance to the NAIC P&C annual statement blank page by page
actions: Import the certified trial balance into the NAIC annual statement software and refresh the account-to-line mapping against the current-year NAIC Annual Statement Instructions for the Property & Casualty blank.

Populate Assets (Page 2), Liabilities/Surplus (Page 3), the Statement of Income (Page 4) and the Cash Flow (Page 5), confirming mortgage guaranty business lands on the Mortgage Guaranty line of the Underwriting and Investment Exhibit.
Flag every new GL account opened during the year that has no blank mapping and get the mapping decision from the Controller before proceeding.
Print the mapping report and file it as the audit trail behind each populated page.
checklist.done: every trial balance account maps to a named annual statement line, with new accounts mapped by documented Controller decision.

checklist.step: Roll forward the statutory contingency reserve and mortgage guaranty specific entries
actions: Build the contingency reserve roll-forward under SSAP No. 58: opening balance, current-year additions of 50% of earned premium, releases of contributions that have completed their 10-year holding period, and any release approved by the domiciliary regulator.
Tie the closing contingency reserve to the liability posted in the general ledger and to the surplus reconciliation, explaining any difference to the cent.
Recompute the premium deficiency reserve test and unearned premium on the mortgage guaranty book and post any required entry before the ledger is re-locked.
Send the roll-forward to the Controller and the Appointed Actuary for concurrence and attach it to the blank workpaper set.
checklist.done: the contingency reserve roll-forward ties to the ledger and to surplus, with Controller and Appointed Actuary concurrence on file.

checklist.step: Load loss and LAE reserves and build Schedule P from the actuarial extract
actions: Deliver the December 31 reserve extract by accident year for the mortgage guaranty line: case reserves, IBNR, paid losses, defensive costs and salvage/subrogation.
Load the extract into the Schedule P triangles in the annual statement software and confirm the paid and incurred rows tie to Page 4 losses incurred and to the ledger loss reserve balance.
Reconcile the reserve extract to the delinquency inventory from the master policy servicing data — number of loans in default, default rate and claim rate assumption — and document the bridge.
Hand the signed reserve report to the Statutory Reporting Manager and the Appointed Actuary.
checklist.done: Schedule P ties to the ledger loss reserves and to the delinquency inventory, with a documented reconciliation bridge.

checklist.step: Obtain the Statement of Actuarial Opinion and the supporting actuarial report
actions: Perform the reserve adequacy review on the mortgage guaranty reserves and the contingency reserve position, documenting the range and the point estimate.

Issue the Statement of Actuarial Opinion in the NAIC-prescribed format with the relevant comment paragraph on mortgage guaranty risk concentration, and the Actuarial Opinion Summary for the domiciliary regulator.
Confirm the reserve amounts opined on equal the amounts carried on Page 3 and in Schedule P to the dollar, and note any difference in the opinion.
Sign and date the opinion and deliver it to the Statutory Reporting Manager for attachment to the March 1 filing.
checklist.done: a signed Statement of Actuarial Opinion exists, the opined reserves equal the carried reserves, and the Actuarial Opinion Summary is prepared.

checklist.step: Prepare the consolidated GAAP financial statements for the non-public approved insurer
actions: Run the GAAP consolidation for the holding company and its insurance subsidiaries and produce the balance sheet, statement of operations, comprehensive income, changes in equity and cash flows.

Draft the footnotes that PMIERs reviewers read first: insurance reserves, reinsurance and quota share cessions, investment portfolio by credit quality, statutory capital and dividend restrictions, and the mortgage guaranty risk-in-force concentration disclosure.

Prepare the statutory-to-GAAP surplus bridge (contingency reserve, deferred acquisition costs, non-admitted assets, deferred tax) so a reader can move from the convention statement to the GAAP equity balance.
Give the draft to the external audit engagement partner and to the Chief Financial Officer for review.
checklist.done: draft consolidated GAAP financial statements with footnotes and a statutory-to-GAAP surplus bridge are in the auditor's hands.

checklist.step: Validate the annual statement and clear every NAIC cross-check
actions: Run the annual statement software validation and work the cross-check exception list to zero unexplained items, page by page.
Confirm the jurat page carries the correct NAIC company code, FEIN, domiciliary state and the officers who will sign, and that Schedule T states agree to the active licence list.

Verify Schedule F (reinsurance), Schedule D (investments) and Schedule Y (holding company organisational chart) agree to the ceded reinsurance system, the investment accounting records and the current corporate structure.
Document every cross-check overridden with a written explanation and Controller approval.
checklist.done: the validation report shows zero unexplained cross-check failures and every override carries a written Controller approval.

checklist.step: Tie the PMIERs Available Assets and Minimum Required Assets disclosure to the filed statement
actions: Pull the December 31 Available Assets calculation under PMIERs Section 703 and reconcile each asset class back to Schedule D and the cash lines on Page 2 of the annual statement.

Recompute Minimum Required Assets as the greater of the aggregate risk-based required asset amount from the PMIERs Exhibit A factor tables and the $400 million floor, and compute the resulting PMIERs sufficiency ratio.
Document the Section 701 sources and diversification of capital position — parent contributions, debt, reinsurance credit — and confirm it agrees with the equity roll-forward in the GAAP statements.
Hand the reconciled capital exhibit to the Controller for inclusion in the Enterprise package.
checklist.done: Available Assets reconcile to Schedule D and Page 2, MRA and the sufficiency ratio are recomputed, and the Section 701 capital narrative agrees to the GAAP equity roll-forward.

checklist.step: File the annual convention statement with the NAIC and the states by March 1
actions: Generate the annual statement filing file and upload it to the NAIC iSite+ Financial Data Repository for the December 31 year end, attaching the Statement of Actuarial Opinion.
File the hard-copy or electronic statement with the domiciliary regulator and every state that requires a direct copy, per that state's filing checklist.
Download and save the NAIC filing receipt and each state acknowledgement as the proof of timely filing.
Record the filing date, statement type and receipt reference on the filing calendar row for the reporting year.
checklist.done: the annual statement is filed by March 1 with NAIC and state receipts saved against the calendar row.

checklist.step: Assemble the Section 802 annual report package for each Enterprise
actions: Build one package per Enterprise containing: the audited consolidated GAAP financial statements with the auditor's opinion, the annual convention statement exactly as filed with the state regulators, the Statement of Actuarial Opinion, and the year's regulator correspondence log.
Add the capital exhibit showing Available Assets, Minimum Required Assets and the sufficiency ratio at December 31 tied to the filed statement.
Name every file to the Enterprise's convention (<insurer NAIC code>_<reporting year>_<document type>.pdf) and confirm each PDF is text-searchable and unwatermarked.
Run the completeness checklist against the Section 802 deliverable list and mark any item still open with its owner and expected date.
checklist.done: a complete, correctly named package exists for Fannie Mae and for Freddie Mac with the completeness checklist fully ticked.

checklist.step: Review and sign the Section 802 transmittal
actions: Review the package against the filed convention statement and the audited GAAP statements and confirm the reported surplus, Available Assets and risk-in-force figures agree across all three.
Read the correspondence log for any unresolved state regulator matter that must be disclosed to the Enterprises and confirm it is described in the transmittal letter.
Sign the transmittal letter certifying the enclosed statements are the ones filed with the state insurance regulators for the year ended December 31.
Return the signed letter to the Regulatory Reporting Manager no later than April 8.
checklist.done: a CFO-signed transmittal letter is on file by April 8 and the reported figures agree across the GAAP, statutory and capital exhibits.

checklist.step: Transmit the package to both Enterprises by April 15 and capture confirmations
actions: Send each Enterprise's package through the agreed Approved Insurer secure transmission channel to the named relationship manager, with the CFO transmittal letter as the cover document.
Request and save a written receipt acknowledgement from each Enterprise, or capture the portal submission confirmation screen with its timestamp.
Post the transmission date, channel, recipient and confirmation reference to the PMIERs filing calendar row for Section 802.
Escalate to the Controller the same business day if either Enterprise has not acknowledged receipt within 3 business days.
checklist.done: both Enterprises have acknowledged receipt on or before April 15 and the confirmations are attached to the calendar row.

checklist.step: Log and clear Enterprise follow-up questions on the annual report
actions: Open a tracker item for every Enterprise question on the annual package, recording the Enterprise, the question text, the date received and the response due date.

Route reserve questions to the Reserving Actuary, capital and investment questions to the Head of Capital Management, and accounting questions to the Controller, with a 5 business day internal turnaround.
Have the Controller review each response for consistency with the filed statement before it is sent, and attach the sent response to the tracker item.
Close the item only when the Enterprise confirms the matter is resolved.
checklist.done: every Enterprise question has a tracker item, a Controller-reviewed response and a written Enterprise closure.

checklist.step: Retain the annual reporting record for the retention period
actions: File the filed convention statement, NAIC receipt, audited GAAP financial statements, actuarial opinion, capital exhibit, transmittal letter and Enterprise confirmations under REG-050 / Section 802 / reporting year.
Apply the 7-year retention label and set the record as read-only so post-filing edits are impossible.
Confirm the repository index makes the record searchable by reporting year, Enterprise and document type.
Record the archive location on the PMIERs filing calendar row so an examiner request can be answered without a search.
checklist.done: the complete annual reporting record is archived read-only under a 7-year label and indexed by year, Enterprise and document type.

testing.step: Build the population of Section 802 annual deliverables
actions: List every component PMIERs Section 802 requires for the reporting year — audited consolidated GAAP financial statements, the filed convention statement, the actuarial opinion and the annual correspondence — for each of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac.
Extract from the document repository every file actually delivered in the package, with its file hash and delivery date.
Reconcile the delivered inventory to the required list and record any missing, extra or superseded document as an immediate exception.
Sign the population as complete before any sampling begins.
testing.done: a signed deliverable population reconciled item-by-item to the Section 802 requirement list exists.

testing.step: Reconcile the delivered statements to the source of record
actions: Download the annual statement as accepted by the NAIC iSite+ Financial Data Repository and compare it page by page to the copy sent to the Enterprises.
Confirm total admitted assets, total liabilities, policyholders' surplus and the contingency reserve balance are identical in both copies.
Compare the audited GAAP financial statements delivered to the Enterprises against the signed set issued by the external auditor, including the opinion date.
Treat any difference between the delivered and filed versions as a fail, not a version-control note.
testing.done: the delivered statements are byte-for-figure identical to the NAIC-accepted statement and the auditor-issued GAAP set.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of annual statement lines and disclosures
actions: Take 100% of the high-risk lines: contingency reserve, loss and LAE reserves, unearned premium, Available Assets components and risk-in-force.
Draw 20 further lines at random from the remaining populated annual statement lines using a recorded, reproducible seed.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and selector name in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn on demand.
Publish the sample list to the Internal Auditor before any re-performance starts.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all high-risk lines plus 20 random lines is documented with its seed and selection date.

testing.step: Re-perform the trial balance to blank mapping for the sample
actions: For each sampled line, pull the underlying GL accounts from the certified December 31 trial balance and total them independently in the audit workpaper.
Compare the independent total to the amount reported on the annual statement page and explain any difference above $50,000.
Open the mapping report and confirm the accounts rolled into the line are the ones the current NAIC Annual Statement Instructions prescribe for that line.
Record every mapping difference as an exception, including cases where the amount is right but the account population is wrong.
testing.done: each sampled line is independently re-totalled from the trial balance and agrees to the filed amount within the $50,000 threshold.

testing.step: Recompute the contingency reserve roll-forward
actions: Independently compute the current-year contingency reserve addition as 50% of earned premium from the Underwriting and Investment Exhibit and compare it to the posted addition.
Recompute the releases by checking each released contribution layer completed its 10-year holding period, and confirm any early release carries written domiciliary regulator approval.
Tie the recomputed closing balance to the Page 3 liability and to the surplus reconciliation.
Log any unsupported release as a statutory accounting exception and notify the Controller the same day.
testing.done: the recomputed contingency reserve balance agrees to the filed Page 3 liability and every release is supported by holding period or regulator approval.

testing.step: Re-perform the Available Assets and Minimum Required Assets tie-out
actions: Rebuild Available Assets from Schedule D and the cash lines of the filed statement without reference to the preparer's workbook, applying the PMIERs Section 703 asset eligibility rules.
Recompute Minimum Required Assets from the Exhibit A risk-based required asset factors and confirm the reported figure is the greater of that amount and the $400 million floor.
Recompute the sufficiency ratio and compare it to the figure delivered to the Enterprises.
Any difference in the sufficiency ratio of more than 0.5 percentage points is escalated to the Chief Financial Officer the same day.
testing.done: independently rebuilt Available Assets, MRA and sufficiency ratio agree with the figures delivered to the Enterprises within 0.5 percentage points.

testing.step: Trace the delivery of each package component to a dated confirmation
actions: For each Enterprise, open the transmission record and read the channel, recipient, timestamp and the acknowledgement reference.
Confirm the acknowledged file names and hashes match the package inventory built in step 1.
Confirm the CFO transmittal letter carries a signature date on or before April 8 and covers the reporting year ended December 31.
Capture the confirmation evidence into the workpaper as a dated screenshot or saved acknowledgement email.
testing.done: every package component traces to a dated Enterprise acknowledgement covering the same file inventory.

testing.step: Recompute the deadline maths for the reporting cycle
actions: Recompute each cycle deadline from the December 31 reporting year end: annual statement March 1, actuarial opinion March 1, Mortgage Guaranty Insurance Supplement April 1, Section 802 Enterprise package April 15.
Compare each recomputed date with the actual completion date evidenced by the NAIC receipt, the signed opinion and the Enterprise acknowledgement.
Compute the slack or overrun in calendar days for each milestone and chart it against the prior two reporting years.
Flag any milestone completed on the deadline date itself as a timeliness risk even where it passed.
testing.done: every milestone has a recomputed deadline, an actual date and a calendar-day variance recorded in the workpaper.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception describing the annual statement line or package component, the difference found and the PMIERs Section 802 impact.
Assign a root cause from the standard set — unmapped new GL account, stale blank instructions, late actuarial extract, missed Enterprise channel change — and an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date before the next quarterly PMIERs submission and require an amended filing plan where the filed statement itself is wrong.
Carry every open exception into next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has a tracker issue, a named root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate over the sampled lines and compare it to the zero-late-delivery and $100,000 reconciliation thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind it.
Have the reviewer who prepared none of the tested statements sign the workpaper, and confirm segregation in the sign-off note.
Report the conclusion and any open breach to the Audit Committee at its next meeting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and Audit Committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

checklist.step: Confirm the Available Asset phase-in step in force for the quarter
actions: Read the FHFA/Enterprises 2024 PMIERs amendment schedule and identify the phase-in step applicable to this quarter-end on the 24-month glide path ending September 30, 2026.

Record the haircut percentages in force this quarter for each asset bucket — cash and short-term, US Treasury and agency, investment-grade corporate bonds by rating band, and assets backed by residential mortgages or commercial real estate.
Confirm with each Enterprise's Approved Insurer contact in writing that no interim guidance changed the step, and file the reply.
Publish the quarter's factor table to the Capital Management workspace and freeze it before classification starts.
checklist.done: the quarter's phase-in step and per-bucket haircut table are published, frozen and confirmed with both Enterprises.

checklist.step: Close the investment book and extract CUSIP-level holdings
actions: Complete the quarter-end investment accounting close and lock the portfolio, confirming trade date positions, accruals and amortised cost are final.
Export the holdings file at CUSIP level with book/adjusted carrying value, fair value, NAIC designation, external credit ratings, asset type, sector and maturity.
Reconcile the extract's total carrying value to the investment control account in the general ledger and clear any difference above $25,000 before release.
Deliver the locked extract to Capital Management with a signed completeness statement.
checklist.done: a locked CUSIP-level holdings extract reconciled to the GL investment control account is delivered with a completeness statement.

checklist.step: Classify every holding by credit quality and liquidity under the amended standard
actions: Assign every CUSIP to an Available Asset bucket using the amended standard's credit quality bands and liquidity tests, recording the rating source and rating date used for each bond.
Where ratings from Moody's, S&P and Fitch differ, apply the documented tie-break rule (second-lowest rating) and note the decision on the row.
Tag every holding backed by residential mortgages or commercial real estate — RMBS, CMBS, mortgage loans, real estate equity — as these carry the amendment's specific limits.
Route any CUSIP that cannot be classified from available data to the Investment Analyst for security-master research and hold it out of Available Assets until resolved.
checklist.done: every CUSIP carries a bucket, a rating source and date, a mortgage/CRE flag, and no unclassified holding is counted as available.

checklist.step: Apply the concentration limits on mortgage and real-estate backed assets
actions: Total the carrying value of the RMBS, CMBS and commercial-real-estate-backed holdings tagged in the prior step.
Compute each category against its limit under the amended standard and record the headroom or excess in dollars and as a percentage of total Available Assets.
Exclude any excess above the limit from Available Assets and show the excluded amount as a separate reconciling line rather than netting it silently.
Notify the Chief Investment Officer where headroom is under 10% so portfolio positioning can be adjusted before the next quarter.
checklist.done: the mortgage/CRE concentration test is computed, any excess is excluded on a visible reconciling line, and thin headroom is escalated to the CIO.

checklist.step: Compute Available Assets and the PMIERs sufficiency ratio
actions: Apply this quarter's phase-in haircuts bucket by bucket to the classified holdings and add eligible cash and receivables to produce Available Assets under Section 703.
Take the Minimum Required Assets figure from the loan-level Exhibit A risk-based calculation and confirm it is the greater of that amount and the $400 million floor.
Compute the sufficiency ratio (Available Assets ÷ Minimum Required Assets) and compare it to the prior quarter, explaining any movement greater than 5 percentage points.
Where the ratio is below 100%, open the 30-calendar-day shortfall notification clock immediately and alert the CFO the same day.
checklist.done: Available Assets, MRA and the sufficiency ratio are computed with a movement explanation, and any sub-100% result has started the 30-day clock.

checklist.step: Reconcile Available Assets to the statutory investment schedules
actions: Bridge total Available Assets to Schedule D Part 1 (bonds), Schedule DA (short-term) and the cash lines of the quarterly statement, line by line.
Show each reconciling item explicitly: ineligible asset classes, phase-in haircuts, concentration exclusions and non-admitted assets.
Confirm NAIC designations used in the classification agree with the designations reported on Schedule D for the same CUSIPs.
Have the Controller review and initial the bridge before either filing is released.
checklist.done: a line-by-line bridge from Schedule D and cash to Available Assets exists with every reconciling item named and Controller initials on it.

checklist.step: Prepare and validate the NAIC quarterly statement
actions: Load the quarter-end trial balance into the quarterly statement blank and populate Assets, Liabilities and Surplus, the Statement of Income and the investment schedules.
Update the contingency reserve balance for the quarter's 50%-of-earned-premium addition and any completed 10-year releases.
Run the software validation and clear the cross-check exception list, documenting any override with Controller approval.
Circulate the draft to the Controller and the Reserving Actuary for review no later than quarter-end plus 30 days.
checklist.done: a validated quarterly statement with zero unexplained cross-check failures is reviewed by the Controller and the Reserving Actuary by day 30.

checklist.step: Assemble the PMIERs quarterly submission for each Enterprise
actions: Build the quarterly package: the Available Asset schedule with the phase-in step applied, the Minimum Required Assets calculation, the sufficiency ratio, and the Exhibit F quarterly portfolio loan-level dataset for the insured portfolio.

Validate the Exhibit F file against the Enterprise layout — record count, loan identifier, LTV, credit score, coverage percentage, delinquency status and coverage effective date — and reject the file on any layout error rather than filing it.
Reconcile the Exhibit F risk-in-force total to the risk-in-force reported in the quarterly statement and document the bridge.
Run the package completeness checklist and mark any open item with owner and expected date, escalating anything still open at day 35.
checklist.done: a layout-valid Exhibit F and capital schedule set exists for each Enterprise, with risk-in-force reconciled to the quarterly statement.

checklist.step: Run the data quality gate on the loan-level dataset
actions: Execute the Exhibit F validation suite: null checks on mandatory fields, referential checks of loan identifiers against the master policy inventory, range checks on LTV and credit score, and duplicate loan identifier detection.
Compare the loan count and aggregate insurance-in-force to the prior quarter and investigate any movement greater than 3% not explained by new insurance written, cancellations and claims.
Route every failed record to the Policy Administration Analyst owning the source field with a same-quarter correction deadline.
Publish the data quality certificate — records in, records failed, records corrected, records excluded — into the submission package.
checklist.done: the validation suite has run, quarter-over-quarter movement is explained, and a data quality certificate is attached to the submission.

checklist.step: File the NAIC quarterly statement within 45 days of quarter-end
actions: Generate the quarterly filing file and upload it to the NAIC iSite+ Financial Data Repository for the quarter ended, on or before May 15, August 15 or November 15 as applicable.
File the copies each state requires directly per that state's quarterly filing checklist.
Save the NAIC filing receipt and every state acknowledgement against the filing calendar row for the quarter.
Escalate to the Controller within one business day if any upload rejects, and re-file the same day the rejection is corrected.
checklist.done: the quarterly statement is accepted by NAIC on or before the 45-day deadline with receipts saved to the calendar row.

checklist.step: Obtain officer review and sign-off on the capital submission
actions: Review the Available Asset schedule, the applied phase-in step, the concentration test and the sufficiency ratio against the prior quarter and the plan.
Confirm with the Head of Capital Management that no asset excluded by the amended standard has been counted and that the mortgage/CRE limits hold.
Sign the quarterly capital submission cover certification no later than quarter-end plus 40 days.
Where the sufficiency ratio is below 100%, approve the shortfall notification and the remediation plan in the same sitting.
checklist.done: the CFO has signed the capital submission by day 40, with any shortfall notification and remediation plan approved at the same time.

checklist.step: Transmit the PMIERs quarterly submission and capture confirmations
actions: Send each Enterprise's capital schedule and Exhibit F dataset through the agreed Approved Insurer secure transmission channel, on or before quarter-end plus 45 calendar days.
Capture the portal or transfer confirmation with its timestamp and file size, and request written acknowledgement from the relationship manager.
Record the submission date, channel, file names and confirmation reference on the PMIERs filing calendar row for the quarter.
Escalate to the CFO the same business day if either Enterprise has not acknowledged within 3 business days of the deadline.
checklist.done: both Enterprises acknowledge receipt on or before quarter-end plus 45 days, with confirmations attached to the calendar row.

checklist.step: Serve any shortfall notification within 30 calendar days
actions: Where the sufficiency ratio falls below 100% at any measurement point, draft the notification to both Enterprises stating the shortfall amount, the driver and the date identified.
Set out the remediation plan with dated actions — parent capital contribution, reinsurance transaction, portfolio repositioning — and the projected ratio after each action.
Send the notification within 30 calendar days of identification and record the send date against the opened clock.
Brief the Board Governance Lead so the shortfall and plan are minuted at the next board meeting.
checklist.done: any shortfall is notified to both Enterprises within 30 calendar days with a dated remediation plan and board briefing.

checklist.step: Clear Enterprise queries on the quarterly submission
actions: Open a tracker item for each Enterprise question, recording the Enterprise, the data field or schedule queried, receipt date and response due date.

Route asset classification questions to Capital Management, loan-level data questions to the Data Quality Analyst, and statutory presentation questions to the Statutory Reporting Manager, with a 5 business day internal turnaround.
Where a query proves a reporting error, prepare the corrected file and resubmit through the same channel with a change note listing the fields restated.
Close the item only on written Enterprise confirmation that the matter is resolved.
checklist.done: every Enterprise query has a tracker item, a routed owner, a resubmission where needed and a written Enterprise closure.

checklist.step: Archive the quarter's filing evidence
actions: File the frozen phase-in factor table, CUSIP classification file, concentration test, Available Asset bridge, NAIC receipt, Exhibit F file and Enterprise confirmations under REG-050 / quarter.
Apply the 7-year retention label and set the record read-only so post-submission edits are impossible.
Confirm the record is indexed by quarter, Enterprise and submission type so an examiner request is answered without a search.
Note the archive reference on the filing calendar row and close the quarter.
checklist.done: the quarter's complete filing record is archived read-only under a 7-year label and referenced from the calendar row.

testing.step: Build the population of quarterly filings and holdings
actions: List every required quarterly filing for the year — three NAIC quarterly statements plus four PMIERs quarterly submissions to each Enterprise — and mark each as made or missing.
Extract the CUSIP-level holdings file used for each quarter's Available Asset calculation, with record counts and total carrying value.
Reconcile the holdings record count and total to the investment book of record snapshot for the same quarter-end date and resolve any difference before sampling.
Sign the population as complete and attach the reconciliation to the workpaper.
testing.done: a signed filing and holdings population reconciled to the investment book of record exists for every quarter.

testing.step: Reconcile Available Assets to the filed statutory schedules
actions: Download the quarterly statement as accepted by NAIC iSite+ and total Schedule D Part 1, Schedule DA and the cash lines independently.
Rebuild the bridge to the Available Assets figure reported to the Enterprises and confirm every reconciling item is named and supported.
Confirm the NAIC designations used in the classification match the designations reported on the filed Schedule D for the same CUSIPs.
Treat any unexplained difference above $1 million as a fail rather than a presentation matter.
testing.done: the reported Available Assets reconcile to the accepted statutory schedules with no unexplained difference above $1 million.

testing.step: Draw the classification sample and document the method
actions: Take 100% of holdings tagged as backed by residential mortgages or commercial real estate, and 100% of holdings whose bucket changed from the prior quarter.
Draw 40 further CUSIPs at random from the remaining holdings using a recorded, reproducible seed, stratified so each credit quality band is represented.
Record the seed, the population size and value, the strata and the selection date in the workpaper.
Publish the sample to the Internal Auditor before any re-performance begins.
testing.done: a reproducible, stratified sample covering all mortgage/CRE and reclassified holdings is documented with its seed.

testing.step: Re-perform the credit quality and liquidity classification
actions: For each sampled CUSIP, pull the security description, asset type and current agency ratings as at the quarter-end date, without first reading the preparer's classification.
Reach an independent bucket conclusion under the amended Available Asset standard, applying the second-lowest-rating tie-break where ratings differ.
Compare to the recorded bucket; treat a right bucket reached from a stale or wrong rating date as an exception in its own right.
Capture the security detail screen for each sampled CUSIP into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled CUSIP has an independent bucket conclusion and a captured source screen, with differences logged.

testing.step: Recompute the phase-in haircuts and the concentration limits
actions: Confirm the phase-in step applied is the one in force at the quarter-end date on the 24-month glide path to September 30, 2026, by reference to the amendment schedule.
Reapply the per-bucket haircuts to the full classified holdings file independently and compare the resulting Available Assets to the reported figure.
Recompute the RMBS, CMBS and commercial-real-estate concentration totals against their limits and confirm any excess was excluded, not netted.
Escalate a wrong phase-in step to the CFO immediately — it misstates every subsequent quarter until corrected.
testing.done: the phase-in step, haircuts and concentration exclusions are independently recomputed and agree with the reported Available Assets.

testing.step: Re-perform the sufficiency ratio and the floor test
actions: Recompute Minimum Required Assets from the loan-level Exhibit A risk-based factors on the quarter's Exhibit F dataset.
Confirm the reported MRA is the greater of that amount and the $400 million floor, and that the floor was actually tested rather than assumed.
Recompute the sufficiency ratio and compare it to the figure submitted to both Enterprises.
Any recomputed ratio below 100% that was reported above 100% is a reportable breach, escalated to the Chief Audit Executive the same day.
testing.done: MRA, the floor test and the sufficiency ratio are independently recomputed and agree with the submitted figures.

testing.step: Trace each filing to a dated regulator or Enterprise confirmation
actions: For each quarter, open the NAIC filing receipt and read the accepted date and statement type.
Open each Enterprise transmission record and read the channel, file names, timestamp and acknowledgement reference.
Confirm the acknowledged Exhibit F file name and record count match the data quality certificate issued for that quarter.
Capture each confirmation into the workpaper as dated evidence.
testing.done: every quarterly filing traces to a dated NAIC receipt and a matching Enterprise acknowledgement.

testing.step: Recompute the 45-day and 30-day clocks
actions: For each quarter, recompute quarter-end plus 45 calendar days and compare it to the actual NAIC acceptance date and the Enterprise acknowledgement date.
For any sufficiency shortfall identified in the year, recompute identification date plus 30 calendar days and compare it to the date the notification was sent to each Enterprise.
Record the slack or overrun in calendar days for each clock and flag any submission landing on the deadline date itself as a timeliness risk.
Confirm the calendar reminders at day 10, 20, 30, 40 and 45 actually fired, from the calendar audit log.
testing.done: every 45-day and 30-day clock is recomputed against actual dates, with reminder firing evidenced from the calendar log.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the quarter, the CUSIP or filing affected, the dollar impact on Available Assets and the PMIERs consequence.
Assign a root cause from the standard set — stale rating data, wrong phase-in step, missed mortgage/CRE tag, late investment close, Exhibit F layout failure — and an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date before the next quarterly submission and require a resubmission plan wherever the filed figure is wrong.
Carry every open exception into the following quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception carries an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date, resubmission decision and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the classification exception rate and the dollar impact on Available Assets, and compare both to the $1 million and zero-late-filing thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind it.
Have a reviewer outside Capital Management and Investment Operations sign the workpaper and record the segregation statement.
Report the conclusion and any breach to the Audit Committee and the Chief Financial Officer, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with an exception rate, dollar impact and stated conclusion is filed and reported to the Audit Committee.

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual with the April 1 supplement deadline; the test runs each April after filing, with an added phase-in verification in any year the Available Asset glide path steps up through September 30, 2026

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Filed supplements with NAIC receipts, the cross-tie matrix, and the PMIERs Available Asset schedule with CUSIP-level support, producible to a state examiner or an Enterprise reviewer within 5 business days

checklist.step: Refresh the schedule inventory from the current NAIC instructions
actions: Open the current-year NAIC Annual Statement Instructions supplement list for the Property & Casualty blank and mark every supplement applicable to a mortgage guaranty writer, including the Mortgage Guaranty Insurance Supplement.
Compare against last year's filed set and list every supplement added, removed or re-formatted for the reporting year.
Add the PMIERs schedules — the Section 703 Available Asset schedule and the Exhibit A risk-based required asset schedule — to the same inventory so nothing is prepared off-book.
Assign each schedule an owner and a February 10 draft date and publish the inventory to the close workspace.
checklist.done: an owner-assigned schedule inventory reflecting this year's NAIC instruction changes and the PMIERs schedules is published.

checklist.step: Prepare the Mortgage Guaranty Insurance Supplement
actions: Populate the supplement from the policy administration and ledger data: direct and assumed risk in force, policies in force, new insurance written, contingency reserve activity and the risk-to-capital calculation.
Compute the risk-to-capital ratio as net risk in force divided by policyholders' position and compare it to the 25:1 statutory limit applied in the domiciliary state.
Tie risk in force in the supplement to the risk in force reported in the PMIERs Exhibit F loan-level dataset for the same date and document the bridge.
Route to the Controller with the supporting extracts attached.
checklist.done: the supplement is populated, the risk-to-capital ratio is computed against the 25:1 limit, and risk in force ties to Exhibit F.

checklist.step: Build the PMIERs Available Asset schedule at CUSIP level
actions: Export the December 31 holdings with CUSIP, carrying value, fair value, NAIC designation, agency ratings, asset type and liquidity classification.

Assign each holding to an Available Asset bucket under the amended standard's credit quality and liquidity distinctions, and tag every holding backed by residential mortgages or commercial real estate.
Apply the phase-in haircuts in force at December 31 on the 24-month glide path to September 30, 2026, and show the pre-haircut and post-haircut totals side by side.
Present the mortgage/CRE concentration test with the limit, the actual, the headroom and any excluded excess as its own line.
checklist.done: a CUSIP-level Available Asset schedule exists showing buckets, ratings, applied phase-in haircuts and the concentration test with excluded excess shown separately.

checklist.step: Build the Exhibit A risk-based required asset schedule
actions: Join the December 31 insured loan inventory to the PMIERs Exhibit A factor tables on the driver attributes — original LTV band, credit score band, loan vintage, performing versus non-performing status and coverage percentage.
Apply the prescribed multipliers and any applicable adjustment factors, and sum the per-loan required asset amounts to the portfolio total.
Test the total against the $400 million floor and show which of the two drives Minimum Required Assets.
Publish a factor-band summary showing loan count, insurance in force and required assets per band so the total can be challenged band by band.
checklist.done: the Exhibit A schedule computes required assets per loan and in total, tested against the $400 million floor, with a factor-band summary.

checklist.step: Prepare the investment supplements and tie them to Schedule D
actions: Prepare Schedule D Parts 1 through 6, Schedule DA and Schedule DB from the investment book of record, with acquisition, disposal and amortisation activity for the year.
Confirm each CUSIP's NAIC designation agrees to the designation used in the Available Asset schedule and correct any mismatch at source rather than on the schedule.
Reconcile total invested assets across Schedule D, the Page 2 asset lines and the Available Asset schedule, showing each reconciling item.
Deliver the schedules and the reconciliation to the Statutory Reporting Manager.
checklist.done: the investment schedules reconcile to Page 2 and to the Available Asset schedule with matching NAIC designations throughout.

checklist.step: Prepare the reinsurance schedules and the ceded credit support
actions: Build Schedule F from the ceded reinsurance system: ceded premium, ceded losses, recoverables, funds held and collateral by reinsurer, with the reinsurer's NAIC code and authorised status.
Compute the provision for reinsurance for unauthorised and slow-paying reinsurers and post it to the liability line.
Identify every cession relied on in the PMIERs risk-in-force calculation and confirm the reinsurer and structure are Enterprise-approved, listing the approval reference.
Reconcile ceded balances to the general ledger reinsurance control accounts and clear differences above $25,000.
checklist.done: Schedule F reconciles to the ledger, the provision for reinsurance is computed, and every PMIERs-relied cession carries an Enterprise approval reference.

checklist.step: Prepare the Insurance Expense Exhibit and the Five-Year Historical Data
actions: Allocate expenses to the loss adjustment, other underwriting, investment and acquisition categories using the documented allocation bases and produce the Insurance Expense Exhibit by line of business.
Confirm total expenses in the exhibit equal the Page 4 underwriting expense total to the dollar.
Populate the Five-Year Historical Data page from the four prior filed statements plus the current year, correcting nothing without a documented amended-filing reference.
Attach the allocation methodology memo so an examiner can follow how expenses reached each line.
checklist.done: the expense exhibit ties to Page 4, the five-year page agrees to prior filed statements, and the allocation memo is attached.

checklist.step: Prepare the actuarial supplements and interrogatories
actions: Complete Schedule P interrogatories and the Schedule P reconciliation, confirming paid and incurred data ties to the loss ledger by accident year.
Prepare the Actuarial Opinion Summary for the domiciliary regulator showing the actuary's point estimate, range and the carried reserve.
Complete the general and supplemental interrogatories that touch reserves, reinsurance and the contingency reserve, answering each with a source reference rather than a bare yes/no.
Deliver the set to the Appointed Actuary for review before the March 1 filing.
checklist.done: Schedule P interrogatories, the reconciliation and the Actuarial Opinion Summary are complete and reviewed by the Appointed Actuary.

checklist.step: Run the cross-tie matrix across every schedule and the main blank
actions: Build a matrix listing every schedule, the main statement line it must agree to, the schedule value, the blank value and the difference.

Drive every difference to zero — Schedule F to the ceded liability, Schedule D to Page 2 invested assets, Schedule P to Page 3 loss reserves, the Mortgage Guaranty Supplement risk in force to Exhibit F.
Where a difference is a legitimate presentation difference, record the reason and the instruction reference on the matrix row instead of leaving it blank.
Present the completed matrix to the Controller for review.
checklist.done: the cross-tie matrix shows zero unexplained differences and every explained difference cites an instruction reference.

checklist.step: Validate the supplements in the NAIC software and clear exceptions
actions: Run the supplement validation in the annual statement software and work the exception list to zero unexplained items.
Confirm every supplement carries the correct NAIC company code, reporting year and the 'not applicable' declaration where a supplement is genuinely not required.
Never file a supplement as 'none' without the Controller's written confirmation that the company writes no business of that type.
Print the clean validation report into the workpaper set.
checklist.done: the supplement validation report is clean and every 'not applicable' declaration carries written Controller confirmation.

checklist.step: Obtain Controller review and approval of the schedule set
actions: Review the schedule inventory against the filed set and confirm no required supplement is missing.
Review the cross-tie matrix and challenge any explained difference that lacks an instruction reference.
Review the Available Asset schedule for the applied phase-in step, the mortgage/CRE exclusions and the reconciliation to Schedule D.
Approve the set in writing by March 25 so the April 1 supplements can be filed without a rush.
checklist.done: the Controller has approved the complete schedule set in writing by March 25 with all cross-ties accepted.

checklist.step: File the supplements by the April 1 deadline
actions: Upload the supplemental filing package to the NAIC iSite+ Financial Data Repository on or before April 1 for the reporting year.
File the copies required directly by the domiciliary regulator and any state whose checklist demands the mortgage guaranty supplement.
Save every filing receipt and state acknowledgement against the filing calendar row for the supplements.
Escalate any upload rejection to the Controller the same business day and re-file on correction.
checklist.done: the supplements are accepted by NAIC on or before April 1 with receipts saved to the calendar row.

checklist.step: Attach the PMIERs capital schedules to the Section 802 package
actions: Add the Available Asset schedule, the Exhibit A required-asset schedule and the sufficiency ratio computation to each Enterprise's Section 802 annual package.
Include the Schedule D reconciliation and the factor-band summary so the Enterprise can challenge either side of the ratio.
Confirm the figures in the schedules equal those in the annual capital exhibit already prepared for the package, to the dollar.
Hand the package to the Regulatory Reporting Manager ahead of the April 8 CFO signature gate.
checklist.done: the PMIERs capital schedules are in both Enterprise packages, agree with the annual capital exhibit and are ready by April 8.

checklist.step: Correct and amend any schedule found wrong after filing
actions: Log every post-filing error with the schedule name, the reported and correct values, and the effect on the main statement or the sufficiency ratio.
Decide amend versus correct-next-period against the domiciliary regulator's materiality guidance and record the reasoning.
Where an amendment is required, refile the corrected supplement through iSite+ and notify the domiciliary regulator and, where the PMIERs schedules move, both Enterprises.
Close the issue only when the amended filing receipt and the Enterprise acknowledgement are attached.
checklist.done: every post-filing error has a logged decision, an amended filing where required, and receipts attached before closure.

checklist.step: Archive the schedule set and its supporting extracts
actions: File each filed supplement, the cross-tie matrix, the CUSIP-level Available Asset schedule, the Exhibit A factor-band summary and every filing receipt under REG-050 / supplements / reporting year.
Apply the 7-year retention label and set the records read-only.
Confirm the index makes each schedule retrievable by schedule name, reporting year and filing date.
Record the archive reference on the filing calendar row and close the annual supplement cycle.
checklist.done: the full schedule set and supporting extracts are archived read-only under a 7-year label and retrievable by schedule name and year.

testing.step: Build the population of required schedules and exhibits
actions: Rebuild the required supplement list independently from the current-year NAIC Annual Statement Instructions for a mortgage guaranty writer, and add the PMIERs Section 703 and Exhibit A schedules.
Extract the schedules actually filed from the NAIC filing package and the Enterprise Section 802 package.
Reconcile required to filed and treat any missing schedule, or any 'not applicable' declaration without Controller confirmation, as an immediate exception.
Sign the population as complete before sampling.
testing.done: a signed schedule population reconciled independently to the NAIC instruction list and the PMIERs requirement exists.

testing.step: Reconcile each schedule to the filed annual statement
actions: Download the annual statement and supplements as accepted by NAIC iSite+ rather than working from the preparer's copies.

Independently re-run the cross-ties: Schedule D to Page 2, Schedule F to the ceded liability, Schedule P to Page 3, the Insurance Expense Exhibit to Page 4, and the Mortgage Guaranty Supplement risk in force to Exhibit F.
Confirm each explained difference on the preparer's matrix cites a real instruction reference by reading that instruction.
Treat any tie that does not hold exactly as a fail.
testing.done: every cross-tie is independently re-run against the NAIC-accepted filing and holds exactly or is logged as a fail.

testing.step: Draw the schedule and holdings sample
actions: Take 100% of the PMIERs schedules, the Mortgage Guaranty Insurance Supplement and Schedule F.
Draw 5 further supplements at random from the remaining filed set and 30 CUSIPs at random from the Available Asset schedule using a recorded seed.
Record the seed, population sizes, selection date and selector name in the workpaper.
Publish the sample before any re-performance begins.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all PMIERs schedules plus randomly selected supplements and CUSIPs is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the Available Asset schedule for the sampled holdings
actions: For each sampled CUSIP, pull asset type, agency ratings and liquidity attributes as at December 31 and reach an independent bucket conclusion under the amended standard.
Confirm the mortgage/CRE tag was applied to every holding backed by residential mortgages or commercial real estate in the sample.
Reapply the December 31 phase-in haircut and compare the post-haircut value to the schedule.
Log any bucket, tag or haircut difference with its dollar effect on Available Assets.
testing.done: each sampled CUSIP has an independent bucket, tag and haircut conclusion with dollar differences quantified.

testing.step: Recompute the Exhibit A required assets on a loan sample
actions: Select 60 insured loans stratified across the LTV and credit score bands, including performing and non-performing loans.
Look up each loan's Exhibit A factor from the published tables using the loan's own attributes and recompute the per-loan required asset amount.
Compare to the amount in the company's schedule and investigate any difference, distinguishing a wrong factor from a wrong loan attribute.
Extrapolate the sampled error rate to the portfolio required-asset total and state the estimated misstatement.
testing.done: 60 loans are independently recomputed against the Exhibit A tables with an extrapolated misstatement estimate stated.

testing.step: Verify the $400 million floor test and the phase-in step
actions: Confirm Minimum Required Assets was set to the greater of the aggregate risk-based amount and the $400 million floor, and that the comparison is evidenced rather than assumed.
Confirm the phase-in step applied at December 31 is the one in force on the 24-month glide path to September 30, 2026, by reading the amendment schedule directly.
Recompute the sufficiency ratio from the independently rebuilt numerator and denominator.
Escalate a wrong phase-in step to the Chief Financial Officer immediately, since it repeats across every subsequent schedule.
testing.done: the floor test and phase-in step are independently verified and the recomputed sufficiency ratio agrees with the reported figure.

testing.step: Trace the reinsurance credit relied on in the schedules
actions: For each cession credited in Schedule F and in the PMIERs risk-in-force calculation, open the treaty in the ceded system and read the effective dates, cession percentage and collateral terms.
Confirm the reinsurer is authorised or the collateral supports the credit taken, and that the provision for reinsurance was computed on any unauthorised balance.
Confirm every PMIERs-relied cession carries an Enterprise approval reference and that the approval is still current at December 31.
Log any credit taken without a current approval as a PMIERs exception, not merely a statutory one.
testing.done: every reinsurance credit traces to a treaty, a collateral or authorised status test, and a current Enterprise approval reference.

testing.step: Trace each schedule to its filing receipt and date
actions: Open the NAIC filing receipts for the supplemental package and read the accepted date against the April 1 deadline.
Confirm the PMIERs capital schedules appear in the Enterprise acknowledgements for the April 15 Section 802 delivery.
Recompute the calendar days between the December 31 year end and each filing to quantify slack or overrun.
Capture each receipt into the workpaper as dated evidence.
testing.done: every schedule traces to a dated receipt or acknowledgement with the deadline variance quantified.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the schedule, the misstatement amount and whether it moves the main statement or the sufficiency ratio.
Assign a root cause — stale instruction list, source system mismatch, wrong Exhibit A factor band, missed mortgage/CRE tag, unapproved cession — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and record the amend-versus-next-period decision with its materiality reasoning.
Carry every open exception into the next reporting year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date, amendment decision and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the schedule exception rate and the aggregate misstatement on Available Assets and required assets against the $1 million threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references.
Have a reviewer who prepared none of the tested schedules sign the workpaper with a segregation statement.
Report to the Audit Committee and the Controller, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with the exception rate, aggregate misstatement and a stated conclusion is filed and reported.
