Pass/fail thresholds.value: Any Section 506 plan area not executed in the year is a fail; any high-rated issue open past its remediation date without Audit Committee-approved extension is a fail; a modified audit opinion or an unremediated material weakness is an automatic escalation to FHFA-facing disclosure review

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual (audit cycle and plan year) with quarterly Audit Committee reporting; the quality assurance review of the Section 506 function runs annually in July, and issue-closure testing runs quarterly

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer sits outside Internal Audit and outside Finance, and must not have owned any tested audit issue or prepared any audited statement

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual Section 506 and external audit assurance workpaper (plan coverage matrix, issue-closure re-performance, opinion and filing evidence) in the compliance evidence repository under REG-050 / audit year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Section 506 internal audit charter, Audit Committee-approved plan and minutes, issued audit reports, issue register with closure evidence, and the audited financial report with the June 1 filing receipt — producible to FHFA, an Enterprise or a state examiner within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Chief Audit Executive responds to Enterprise or FHFA questions on the Section 506 function through the Regulatory Reporting Manager; the General Counsel clears any disclosure of an internal control deficiency before it is sent, and the CFO signs any statement about audited financial data

checklist.step: Approve the Section 506 internal audit charter and annual plan
actions: Refresh the internal audit charter against PMIERs Section 506, confirming the function's independence, reporting line to the Audit Committee and unrestricted access to underwriting, QC, claims and finance records.

Build the risk-assessed annual plan showing at least one audit in each Section 506 assurance area: underwriting and loan eligibility, post-closing quality control, claims and rescission practices, and financial reporting including the PMIERs capital calculation.
Present the charter and plan to the Audit Committee for approval before January 1 and record the approval in the minutes.
Load the approved plan into the audit management tool with an owner, quarter and budgeted hours per engagement.
checklist.done: the Audit Committee has approved the charter and a plan covering every Section 506 area before the plan year begins.

checklist.step: Engage the external auditor and fix the statutory and GAAP scope
actions: Confirm the engaged firm is qualified and independent under the NAIC Annual Financial Reporting Model Regulation and that the lead partner rotation requirement is met.
Agree the engagement letter scope: consolidated GAAP financial statements for the non-public approved insurer and the statutory-basis audited financial report for the domiciliary regulator.
Agree the timetable back from the deadlines — draft opinion March 15, signed GAAP statements April 1 for the April 15 Enterprise package, statutory audited report ready May 15 for the June 1 filing.
File the signed engagement letter and notify the domiciliary regulator of the auditor appointment where the state requires it.
checklist.done: a signed engagement letter covers both the GAAP and statutory audits on a timetable that meets April 15 and June 1.

checklist.step: Run the audit readiness assessment before fieldwork
actions: Confirm every balance sheet account reconciliation for December 31 is prepared, reviewed and signed in the close tool, with no aged unreconciled items above $50,000.
Assemble the prepared-by-client package: trial balance, contingency reserve roll-forward, reserve report, investment holdings, Schedule D and F support, and the PMIERs Available Asset schedule.
Walk the auditor through the mortgage guaranty specific balances — contingency reserve, risk in force, delinquency inventory — before fieldwork opens.
Log any missing item with an owner and a date before the auditor arrives rather than during fieldwork.
checklist.done: all reconciliations are signed, the PBC package is complete, and any gap has a named owner and date before fieldwork starts.

checklist.step: Manage the auditor request list through fieldwork
actions: Post every auditor request to the shared request tracker with requester, request date, owner and due date, and never accept requests by ad hoc email.
Provide each item from the system of record with a screenshot or extract showing the source, not a re-keyed summary.
Escalate any request open more than 5 business days to the Controller with the reason.
Keep a copy of every item provided in the audit evidence folder so the same support answers a later examiner request.
checklist.done: every auditor request is tracked, sourced from the system of record and copied into the audit evidence folder.

checklist.step: Support the auditor's testing of the PMIERs capital balances
actions: Walk the auditor through the Available Asset calculation: source holdings, credit quality and liquidity bucketing, the phase-in step in force at December 31 and the mortgage/CRE concentration limits.
Provide the Exhibit A required-asset calculation with the factor tables and the loan attribute source, plus the $400 million floor test.
Answer the auditor's recalculation differences the same week and correct the schedule at source where the auditor is right.
Record every audit adjustment to Available Assets or required assets and assess whether it changes the reported sufficiency ratio.
checklist.done: the auditor has walked and tested the capital calculation, and every adjustment is recorded with its sufficiency ratio effect assessed.

checklist.step: Execute the Section 506 underwriting and quality control audits
actions: Audit loan eligibility decisioning against the master policy and the Enterprise-approved underwriting guidelines, sampling insured loans across delegated and non-delegated channels.
Audit the post-closing quality control process against PMIERs Sections 502-504: sample selection methodology, review completeness, defect classification and rebuttal handling.
Test the Section 402 property valuation controls — appraisal source, review triggers and value reconciliation — on the same loan sample.
Issue the report with rated findings, agreed management actions, owners and dates, and load them to the issue register.
checklist.done: underwriting, QC and property valuation audits are issued with rated findings and dated, owned management actions.

checklist.step: Execute the Section 506 claims and rescission audit
actions: Sample paid, denied, curtailed and rescinded mortgage guaranty claims across the year and re-perform the coverage decision against the master policy terms.
Test that every rescission or claim curtailment followed the documented investigation, notice and appeal steps, and that the servicer was notified within the master policy timeframe.
Reconcile claims paid in the sample to the loss ledger and to the claim payment records, confirming the amounts and dates agree.
Issue findings on any decision unsupported by file evidence and load them to the issue register with owners and dates.
checklist.done: the claims audit re-performs coverage and rescission decisions on a documented sample and issues owned, dated findings.

checklist.step: Execute the Section 506 financial reporting audit
actions: Test the key controls over the statutory close: reconciliation review and approval, journal entry authorisation, the contingency reserve calculation and the annual statement cross-tie review.
Test the controls over the PMIERs quarterly submission: the phase-in factor freeze, the Available Asset classification review and the Exhibit F data quality gate.
Test the completeness and timeliness controls for the April 15 Section 802 delivery and the 30-day shortfall notification path.
Record control design and operating effectiveness conclusions per control in the GRC control library.
checklist.done: each key statutory and PMIERs reporting control has a documented design and operating effectiveness conclusion in the control library.

checklist.step: Clear audit adjustments and sign the management representation letter
actions: Review the auditor's summary of corrected and uncorrected misstatements and confirm each uncorrected item is genuinely immaterial to statutory surplus and to the PMIERs sufficiency ratio.
Confirm the representations on reserves, related parties, subsequent events, litigation and regulatory matters against the compliance and legal registers before signing.
Sign the management representation letter on the date the auditor releases the opinion, not before.
Direct any correction that moves reported Available Assets or required assets back through the capital schedule owner.
checklist.done: the representation letter is signed on the opinion release date with every uncorrected misstatement assessed against surplus and the sufficiency ratio.

checklist.step: Issue the audited financial statements and file the audited report
actions: Obtain the signed auditor's opinion on the consolidated GAAP financial statements by April 1 so the Section 802 package can be delivered by April 15.
Obtain the statutory-basis audited financial report and file it with the domiciliary regulator, and with every state that requires a direct copy, by June 1.
Save the filing receipts and the auditor's communications to those charged with governance against the audit calendar row.
Notify both Enterprises promptly where the opinion is anything other than unmodified.
checklist.done: the GAAP opinion is signed by April 1, the statutory audited report is filed by June 1, and any modified opinion is notified to the Enterprises.

checklist.step: Report audit results to the Audit Committee and the Board
actions: Present each quarter the plan completion percentage, the audits issued, the findings by rating and the ageing of open issues.
Present the external auditor's management letter and the status of each control deficiency, distinguishing significant deficiencies from material weaknesses.
Confirm to the committee that the Section 506 function retained its independence and had unrestricted access during the period, and minute the confirmation.
Post the pack to the board portal and confirm the minutes record the committee's acceptance.
checklist.done: quarterly reporting is minuted with plan completion, findings by rating, issue ageing and an independence confirmation.

checklist.step: Track and validate remediation of audit issues
actions: Maintain the issue register with rating, owner, agreed action, original due date and any approved extension with its reason.
Chase owners at 30 days before due and weekly once overdue, and escalate any high-rated issue overdue by 30 days to the Chief Audit Executive and the Audit Committee.
Require closure evidence — re-performed control, updated procedure, system change reference — and reject a closure supported only by an owner assertion.
Re-test a sample of closed high-rated issues one quarter after closure to confirm the fix held.
checklist.done: every issue carries an owner, dated action and evidenced closure, with high-rated closures re-tested a quarter later.

checklist.step: Run the annual quality assessment of the Section 506 function
actions: Assess the internal audit function against its charter and professional standards: independence, competence, risk-based planning, workpaper quality and reporting.
Confirm the executed plan actually covered every Section 506 assurance area and quantify any area dropped or deferred during the year.
Interview the Audit Committee chair, the Chief Underwriting Officer and the Controller on the function's access, candour and usefulness, and record the responses.
Issue the assessment with recommendations to the Audit Committee and set dates for each.
checklist.done: an annual quality assessment covering independence, plan coverage and stakeholder feedback is issued to the Audit Committee with dated recommendations.

checklist.step: Assemble the audit evidence set for Enterprise and FHFA review
actions: Compile the Section 506 pack: charter, approved plan, issued audit reports, issue register extract, Audit Committee minutes and the quality assessment.
Compile the external audit pack: signed opinions, audited financial report, management letter, representation letter and the June 1 filing receipt.
Redact nothing without General Counsel direction and record any privilege call on the pack index.
Confirm the pack can be produced within 5 business days of an Enterprise or FHFA request and record the test of that retrieval.
checklist.done: a complete, indexed audit evidence pack exists and its 5-business-day retrieval has been tested and recorded.

checklist.step: Archive the audit cycle record
actions: File the opinions, audited statements, representation letter, management letter, internal audit reports and issue register extract under REG-050 / audit / reporting year.
Apply the 7-year retention label and set the records read-only.
Confirm the index makes each item retrievable by audit year, assurance area and issue rating.
Record the archive reference on the audit calendar row and close the cycle.
checklist.done: the full audit cycle record is archived read-only under a 7-year label and retrievable by year, area and rating.

testing.step: Build the population of audits and audit deliverables
actions: Extract the Audit Committee-approved Section 506 plan for the year with every planned engagement and its assurance area.
Extract every audit report actually issued in the year and every external audit deliverable — opinions, audited financial report, management letter, representation letter.
Reconcile planned to issued and list every engagement deferred, dropped or added, with the approval that authorised the change.
Sign the population as complete before sampling.
testing.done: a signed population reconciling the approved plan to issued audits and external deliverables exists.

testing.step: Reconcile plan coverage to the Section 506 assurance areas
actions: Map each issued audit to the Section 506 areas — underwriting, post-closing quality control, claims, financial reporting — and build a coverage matrix.
Confirm every area received at least one audit in the year and that scope statements actually covered the PMIERs-relevant processes, not adjacent ones.
Read the plan-change approvals for any area deferred and confirm the Audit Committee approved the deferral in minutes.
Treat an uncovered area as a fail regardless of the reason given.
testing.done: the coverage matrix shows every Section 506 area audited, or the gap is logged as a fail with the minuted deferral attached.

testing.step: Draw the sample of audits, issues and audit files
actions: Take 100% of high-rated issues raised or closed in the year and 100% of audits covering the PMIERs capital calculation.
Draw 6 further engagements and 25 medium/low issues at random using a recorded, reproducible seed.
Record the seed, population sizes, selection date and selector name in the workpaper.
Publish the sample to the reviewer before re-performance begins.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all high-rated issues and capital-related audits plus random engagements is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform a sampled audit conclusion from the workpapers
actions: For each sampled engagement, read the scope, risk assessment, test steps and sample sizes and judge whether the evidence supports the stated conclusion.

Re-perform two test steps per engagement directly against the source system — the underwriting file in the underwriting platform or the claim file in the claims platform — and compare your result to the auditor's.
Confirm the finding rating matches the rating criteria in the charter and is not softened relative to the evidence.
Log every unsupported conclusion or downgraded rating as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled engagement has an independent re-performance of two test steps and a conclusion-support judgement.

testing.step: Trace issue closures to evidence rather than assertion
actions: For each sampled closed issue, open the closure evidence and confirm it shows the control operating — a re-performed test, an approved procedure version, or a system change reference.
Reject closures supported only by an owner email asserting the fix is done, and reopen them in the register.
Confirm the Chief Audit Executive signed the closure of every high-rated issue.
Re-test one control per closed high-rated issue against the live process to confirm the fix held.
testing.done: every sampled closure is evidenced by operating-control proof and high-rated closures carry a CAE signature and a held re-test.

testing.step: Recompute the audit and filing deadline maths
actions: Recompute the June 1 statutory audited report deadline from the December 31 year end and compare it to the filing receipt date.
Confirm the signed GAAP opinion date is on or before April 1 and that the audited statements delivered by April 15 are the opinion-covered set.
Recompute issue ageing from raise date to due date and to closure date, and recount overdue high-rated issues independently of the register's own ageing column.
Flag any deliverable landing on its deadline date as a timeliness risk even where it passed.
testing.done: every audit deadline is recomputed against actual dates and issue ageing is independently recounted.

testing.step: Verify the independence and access of the Section 506 function
actions: Confirm the Chief Audit Executive reports functionally to the Audit Committee and that the committee approved the plan, budget and any CAE appointment or removal, from the minutes.
Confirm no internal auditor audited a process they operated or managed in the prior 12 months, from the engagement staffing records.
Confirm the external auditor's independence and partner rotation compliance from the engagement letter and the firm's independence confirmation.
Log any impairment of independence or access, including a refused or delayed information request, as an exception.
testing.done: independence and unrestricted access are evidenced from minutes, staffing records and the auditor independence confirmation.

testing.step: Verify the treatment of control deficiencies and audit adjustments
actions: Read the external auditor's management letter and confirm each deficiency is on the issue register with a rating consistent with its description.
Confirm every uncorrected misstatement in the auditor's summary was assessed against statutory surplus and the PMIERs sufficiency ratio, with the assessment documented.
Confirm any correction that moved Available Assets or required assets was pushed back into the capital schedule and, where material, notified to the Enterprises.
Treat a deficiency absent from the register as a fail.
testing.done: every management letter deficiency is registered and every uncorrected misstatement carries a documented surplus and sufficiency ratio assessment.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the engagement or deliverable, the PMIERs Section 506 or Section 802 impact, and the evidence gap.
Assign a root cause — plan area dropped, scope too narrow, unsupported conclusion, closure without evidence, late deliverable, independence impairment — and an owner.
Set a remediation date inside the current plan year and require an added engagement where an assurance area went uncovered.
Carry every open exception into the next annual assessment as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, where coverage failed, an added engagement.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute plan completion, the exception rate on sampled engagements and closures, and the count of overdue high-rated issues against the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion on whether the Section 506 function and the external audit process met the requirement, citing workpaper references.
Have the reviewer — outside Internal Audit and outside Finance — sign the workpaper with a segregation statement.
Report to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper, notifying the Enterprises where a Section 506 area went unaudited.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with plan completion, exception rate and a stated conclusion is filed and reported to the Audit Committee.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Regulatory Reporting Manager owns the PMIERs reporting calendar and the timeliness evidence behind it, including the 45-calendar-day Exhibit B Operational Performance Scorecard data submission to each Enterprise every quarter

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — PMIERs (Sept 27, 2018) Section 802 and Exhibit B Operational Performance Scorecard, re-read against the current PMIERs text and each Enterprise's scorecard data dictionary at the start of every quarter

In-scope processes.value: Calendar maintenance for every PMIERs and statutory obligation of the approved insurer → quarterly capture of the Exhibit B scorecard operational metrics from underwriting, quality control, claims and servicing systems → submission within 45 calendar days of quarter-end → timeliness evidence capture and reporting

In-scope systems.value: Master filing calendar holding every obligation, owner, due-date rule, reminder schedule and submission confirmation; Exhibit B metric data is sourced from the underwriting, claims and servicing platforms into the reporting warehouse

Compliance procedure documented.value: PMIERs Reporting Calendar & Exhibit B Scorecard Procedure — obligation register with due-date rules, escalation ladder, metric definitions per scorecard measure, source system per metric, and the timeliness evidence standard

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer and the Head of Compliance; reviewed each quarter against Enterprise scorecard guidance changes and after any missed or near-missed deadline

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Exhibit B scorecard data within 45 calendar days of each quarter-end (May 15, August 14, November 14, February 14); Exhibit F loan-level dataset on the same 45-day clock; Exhibit E certificate April 15; Section 802 annual package April 15; NAIC quarterly and annual statement dates

Deadline reminders configured.value: Calendar-driven alerts at T-30, T-15, T-7, T-3 and T-1 calendar days to each due date, routed to the obligation owner and their manager, with an automatic escalation to the Chief Financial Officer at T-3 if the item is not at 'ready to submit'

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Per obligation: the calendar row with computed due date, the submitted file, the Enterprise or regulator confirmation with timestamp, and the reminder audit log — retained 7 years in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any submission after the 45-day clock, any calendar row missing a confirmation, and any scorecard metric restated after submission is logged with the days late, the driver and the process fix

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CFO signs off on the root cause and the process fix for every late or restated PMIERs submission before the exception is closed

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every obligation row on the PMIERs and statutory filing calendar for the period, and every Exhibit B scorecard metric submitted to each Enterprise in each of the four quarters

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero submissions after the 45-calendar-day clock and zero calendar rows without a saved confirmation; any scorecard metric whose recomputed value differs from the submitted value by more than 1 percentage point (or 1 business day on a cycle-time measure) is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous with a quarterly 45-day submission; calendar completeness is tested quarterly within 10 business days of the deadline, and the obligation register is re-derived from source in full every January

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly filing calendar and Exhibit B test workpaper (obligation register re-derivation, metric recomputation, timeliness evidence) in the compliance evidence repository under REG-050 / calendar / quarter

checklist.step: Re-derive the PMIERs obligation register from the source requirements
actions: Read the current PMIERs text section by section and list every reporting, certification and notification obligation of the approved insurer, with its section reference.
Add each Enterprise's supplemental reporting instructions and the statutory NAIC dates the approved insurer must also meet.
For each obligation record the due-date rule as a formula — quarter-end plus 45 calendar days, April 15, identification plus 30 calendar days — never as a hard-coded date.
Reconcile the re-derived register to the live calendar and open a gap item for every obligation on one list but not the other.
checklist.done: the obligation register is re-derived from the PMIERs text with formula-based due-date rules and reconciled to the live calendar.

checklist.step: Load obligations onto the calendar with owners and escalation paths
actions: Create one calendar row per obligation per occurrence with the computed due date, named owner, backup owner and the escalation manager.
Attach the run book link, the required file layout and the destination channel for each Enterprise to the row.
Configure reminders at T-30, T-15, T-7, T-3 and T-1 calendar days to the owner and manager, with an automatic CFO escalation at T-3 where status is not 'ready to submit'.
Have each named owner accept their rows in writing at the start of the quarter.
checklist.done: every obligation has a dated calendar row with an accepted owner, backup, escalation path and configured reminders.

checklist.step: Freeze the Exhibit B metric definitions for the quarter
actions: Open each Enterprise's current Exhibit B Operational Performance Scorecard data dictionary and list every metric with its numerator, denominator, population filter and measurement window.
Compare against last quarter's definitions and record every change the Enterprise made, with the effective quarter.
Publish the frozen definition set for the quarter and circulate the changes to the underwriting, quality control, claims and servicing metric owners.
Log a change request wherever a definition change requires a source system field that is not currently captured.
checklist.done: the quarter's Exhibit B metric definitions are frozen, changes are circulated to metric owners, and data gaps are raised as change requests.

checklist.step: Collect the scorecard source data from the operating systems
actions: Run the quarterly extracts feeding the scorecard: underwriting decision events from the underwriting platform, post-closing QC review outcomes, claim receipt-to-decision events from the claims platform and servicer delinquency reporting events.
Stamp each extract with the source system, extraction timestamp, record count and the quarter-end cut-off applied.
Reconcile each extract's record count to the source system's own control report and resolve differences before the data is used.
Publish the extracts into the reporting layer with lineage recorded from source field to scorecard metric.
checklist.done: every scorecard extract is stamped, count-reconciled to its source control report and published with field-level lineage.

checklist.step: Compute the Exhibit B metrics and review the movement
actions: Compute each scorecard metric strictly to the frozen definition — cycle times in the stated unit, defect and error rates as the defined numerator over the defined denominator.
Produce the quarter-over-quarter movement view with the prior four quarters and flag any metric moving more than 10% relative.
Send each flagged metric to its business owner — Underwriting Quality / Audit Manager, Claims Director / Manager or Operations Manager — for a written explanation before submission.
Lock the computed metric set once explanations are attached and version it with the quarter tag.
checklist.done: all scorecard metrics are computed to the frozen definitions, with written owner explanations attached to every flagged movement.

checklist.step: Run the accuracy control over the scorecard submission
actions: Execute the validation suite on the scorecard file: mandatory field completeness, metric value range checks, denominators greater than zero and period alignment to the quarter.
Recompute three metrics independently from the raw extract using a separate query path and compare to the reported values.
Reject the file and return it to the BI Developer on any failed check rather than annotating the exception in the cover note.
Issue the data quality certificate — checks run, checks passed, records excluded and why — into the submission package.
checklist.done: the validation suite has passed, three metrics are independently recomputed, and a data quality certificate is attached.

checklist.step: Assemble and submit the quarterly package within the 45-day clock
actions: Assemble the quarterly submission for each Enterprise: the Exhibit B scorecard data, the Exhibit F loan-level dataset and the data quality certificate.
Compute the due date as quarter-end plus 45 calendar days and target submission at day 40 to leave rejection recovery time.
Transmit through the agreed Approved Insurer channel and capture the confirmation with its timestamp, file names and record counts.
Attach the confirmation to the calendar row and set the row status to submitted the same day.
checklist.done: the quarterly package is transmitted by day 40 with confirmations attached and the calendar row closed as submitted.

checklist.step: Capture the timeliness evidence for every calendar row
actions: For each closed row, file the submitted file, the confirmation with timestamp, and the computed due date so the days-early figure is self-evident.
Export the reminder audit log showing the T-30 through T-1 alerts actually fired and attach it to the row.
Flag any row closed without a confirmation as incomplete and reopen it until evidence exists.
Publish the quarter's timeliness evidence index for the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: every calendar row carries a submitted file, a timestamped confirmation, the computed due date and the reminder audit log.

checklist.step: Operate the escalation ladder on at-risk obligations
actions: Review the calendar dashboard weekly and list every row not at 'ready to submit' inside T-7 calendar days.
Escalate each at-risk row to the owner's manager the same day with the specific blocker and the date it must clear.
Escalate to the Chief Financial Officer at T-3 with a stated recovery plan, and never let a row reach its due date without an escalation record.
Record every escalation, decision and recovery action on the calendar row.
checklist.done: no obligation reaches its due date without an escalation trail, and every at-risk row has a dated recovery plan.

checklist.step: Self-report and correct any late or restated submission
actions: Where a submission passes the 45-day clock, notify both Enterprises with the submission date, the days late, the cause and the corrective action.
Where a submitted metric is later found wrong, resubmit the corrected file with a change note listing every restated metric and its old and new value.
Approve the process fix — additional lead time, source system change, added control — with an implementation date before the next quarter.
Confirm the fix landed by reviewing the next quarter's calendar performance for the same obligation.
checklist.done: every late or restated submission is self-reported, corrected, and closed with a CFO-approved and verified process fix.

checklist.step: Report calendar performance to the compliance governance forum
actions: Produce the quarterly pack: obligations due, submitted on time, submitted late, average days of slack, and every escalation raised.
Show the Exhibit B metric trend against the Enterprise scorecard expectations and highlight any deteriorating measure.
Present open exceptions with owner, cause and remediation date, and repeat any item carried from the prior quarter.
Minute the forum's decisions and load actions into the tracker with owners and dates.
checklist.done: the quarterly calendar performance pack is presented, minuted and its actions loaded to the tracker with owners and dates.

checklist.step: Maintain the calendar against regulatory and organisational change
actions: Monitor FHFA and Enterprise publications for changes to PMIERs reporting content, format or timing, and log each change with its effective date.
Update the affected calendar rows' due-date rules, layouts and run books within 5 business days of a published change.
Reassign rows within 5 business days whenever an owner leaves the role, and obtain the new owner's written acceptance.
Record every calendar change with the change reason, source and approver so the register history is auditable.
checklist.done: regulatory and ownership changes reach the calendar within 5 business days with an auditable change history.

checklist.step: Rehearse the submission run book before each quarter-end
actions: Two weeks before quarter-end, walk the run book with the metric owners, the data engineer and the submitter, timing each step.
Test the transmission channel with a dummy file where the Enterprise supports it, and confirm credentials and file size limits are current.
Identify any step whose duration leaves less than 5 calendar days of buffer before the 45-day deadline and re-sequence it.
Publish the revised run book with the timings and circulate to everyone on the critical path.
checklist.done: the run book is rehearsed and timed each quarter with at least 5 calendar days of buffer before the 45-day deadline.

checklist.step: Preserve the scorecard lineage for regulator inspection
actions: Publish the source-to-report lineage for every Exhibit B metric — source system, source field, transformation and reported metric — into the data catalog.
Version the lineage with the quarter so a reviewer can reconstruct the metric exactly as submitted.
Attach the frozen definition set and the metric computation queries for the quarter to the lineage record.
Test retrieval by asking an uninvolved analyst to reconstruct one metric from the lineage alone, and record the result.
checklist.done: quarter-versioned lineage, definitions and queries exist for every metric, with a successful independent reconstruction recorded.

checklist.step: Archive the quarter's calendar and submission record
actions: File the calendar export, submitted files, confirmations, reminder logs, data quality certificate and metric explanations under REG-050 / calendar / quarter.
Apply the 7-year retention label and set the record read-only.
Confirm the index makes rows retrievable by obligation, quarter, owner and submission date.
Record the archive reference on the calendar rows and close the quarter.
checklist.done: the quarter's calendar and submission record is archived read-only under a 7-year label and retrievable by obligation and quarter.

testing.step: Build the population of obligations and submissions
actions: Export every PMIERs and statutory calendar row due in the period with its computed due date, owner, submission date and confirmation reference.
Independently re-derive the obligation list from the PMIERs text and the Enterprise reporting instructions rather than accepting the register.
Reconcile re-derived to exported and treat any obligation absent from the calendar as an immediate exception.
Sign the population as complete before sampling.
testing.done: a signed obligation population independently re-derived from the PMIERs text and reconciled to the calendar exists.

testing.step: Reconcile submitted scorecard data to the source systems
actions: Pull the raw underwriting, QC, claims and servicing extracts used for the quarter and compare record counts to the source system control reports.
Confirm the quarter-end cut-off applied in the extracts matches the scorecard measurement window in the frozen definitions.
Trace the reported denominator of three metrics back to the underlying record set and count it independently.
Treat any population that cannot be reconciled to a source control report as a fail.
testing.done: the scorecard source extracts reconcile to source control reports and three denominators are independently counted.

testing.step: Draw the sample of calendar rows and metrics
actions: Take 100% of PMIERs Enterprise-facing rows — Exhibit B, Exhibit F, Exhibit E and the Section 802 package — and 100% of metrics that moved more than 10% quarter over quarter.
Draw 15 further calendar rows and 8 further metrics at random using a recorded, reproducible seed.
Record the seed, population sizes, selection date and selector name in the workpaper.
Publish the sample before re-performance begins.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all Enterprise-facing rows and volatile metrics plus random selections is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the sampled Exhibit B metric calculations
actions: Read the frozen definition for each sampled metric and write an independent query against the raw extract without opening the production logic.
Compare the independently computed value to the submitted value and record the difference in percentage points or business days.
Where the values differ, determine whether the cause is the definition, the population filter or the transformation, and state which.
Treat a difference above 1 percentage point, or 1 business day on a cycle-time metric, as a fail.
testing.done: each sampled metric has an independent recomputation, a quantified difference and a stated cause for any difference.

testing.step: Verify the metric definitions used match the Enterprise dictionary
actions: Open the Enterprise's Exhibit B data dictionary in force for the quarter and compare each sampled metric's numerator, denominator, filter and window to the frozen internal definition.
Confirm any Enterprise definition change effective in the quarter was actually applied, not deferred to the next cycle.
Confirm the metric owner's written explanation exists for every flagged movement and is consistent with the underlying data.
Log a definition mismatch as a fail even where the computed value looks reasonable.
testing.done: every sampled definition matches the Enterprise dictionary in force and every flagged movement carries a consistent owner explanation.

testing.step: Trace each sampled obligation to timestamped confirmation evidence
actions: Open each sampled calendar row and read the submitted file, the confirmation timestamp and the file names and record counts acknowledged.
Confirm the acknowledged record count equals the count on the data quality certificate for that submission.
Confirm a row marked submitted actually has a confirmation, and reopen any row where the evidence is only an internal status change.
Capture each confirmation into the workpaper as dated evidence.
testing.done: every sampled row traces to a timestamped external confirmation whose record counts match the data quality certificate.

testing.step: Recompute the 45-day clocks and the reminder firing
actions: Recompute quarter-end plus 45 calendar days for each quarter and compare it to the confirmation timestamp for the Exhibit B and Exhibit F submissions.
Recompute the April 15 and other fixed dates and compare them to the calendar's stored due dates to catch a wrong due-date rule.
Read the reminder audit log and confirm the T-30, T-15, T-7, T-3 and T-1 alerts fired to the named owner and manager.
Flag every submission with less than 3 calendar days of slack as a timeliness risk even where it passed.
testing.done: every due date is recomputed from its rule, compared to the actual submission timestamp, and reminder firing is evidenced.

testing.step: Test the escalation ladder on at-risk rows
actions: Identify every row that was not at 'ready to submit' inside T-7 and read the escalation record on the row.
Confirm the manager escalation happened the same day the row went at-risk and the CFO escalation happened at T-3 where required.
Confirm each escalation names a specific blocker and a dated recovery action, not a status restatement.
Log any at-risk row with no escalation record as a control failure regardless of whether the submission was on time.
testing.done: every at-risk row shows same-day manager escalation, T-3 CFO escalation where required, and a dated recovery action.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the obligation or metric, the days late or the size of the metric difference, and the Enterprise impact.
Assign a root cause — obligation missing from the register, wrong due-date rule, stale metric definition, late source extract, no escalation — and an owner.
Set a remediation date before the next quarterly submission and require an Enterprise self-report where a deadline was missed.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a self-report decision where a deadline was missed.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute on-time submission rate, the count of rows without confirmations and the metric exception rate against the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references.
Have the reviewer, who owns no calendar row and sits outside Regulatory Reporting, sign the workpaper with a segregation statement.
Report to the compliance governance forum and the Chief Financial Officer and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with the on-time rate, metric exception rate and a stated conclusion is filed and reported.

checklist.step: Map every PMIERs-governed area to a named governing document
actions: List the PMIERs sections that require written policies, procedures or practices — Section 302 generally, plus 402 property valuation, 502-504 quality control, 600-601 lender approval and monitoring, 701/703 capital and 800-series reporting.
Map each to the specific document that governs it by document id, version and owner, and mark any section with no governing document as a gap.
Send each gap to the relevant area head — Chief Underwriting Officer, Claims Director / Manager, Head of Capital Management — with a drafting deadline.
Publish the coverage matrix as the single index an Enterprise reviewer would be handed.
checklist.done: every PMIERs section requiring written procedures maps to a named, versioned document or to an owned gap with a drafting deadline.

checklist.step: Set the document standard and the taxonomy
actions: Define the mandatory sections of every Section 302 document: purpose, PMIERs citation, scope, roles and authorities, the step-by-step procedure, controls, records produced and retention.
Require every document to carry document id, version, effective date, owner, approver, review date and a change log with the driver for each change.
Classify documents as policy (what must happen), procedure (how it is done) or practice (evidence of routine execution) so an Enterprise reviewer can navigate the set.
Publish the template and retire any document that does not conform at its next review.
checklist.done: the template, metadata standard and policy/procedure/practice taxonomy are published and applied at every subsequent review.

checklist.step: Refresh the underwriting and loan eligibility procedures
actions: Update the underwriting procedure to match the current Enterprise-eligible loan criteria — LTV limits, credit score floors, documentation requirements, property and occupancy types and ineligible loan features.
Document the delegated underwriting framework: which lenders hold delegated authority, the limits, the monitoring triggers and the process for suspending delegation.
Document the Section 402 property valuation requirements: acceptable valuation sources, review triggers, tolerance for value variance and escalation to a second valuation.
Confirm the written steps match what the underwriting platform actually enforces, and raise a change request wherever the system is more or less permissive than the document.
checklist.done: the underwriting, delegated authority and property valuation procedures are current and reconciled to the system's enforced rules.

checklist.step: Refresh the post-closing quality control procedures
actions: Update the QC procedure to the Sections 502-504 requirements: the random sample methodology and sample size, discretionary sampling triggers, review scope and reviewer independence.
Document the defect taxonomy, the gross and net defect rate definitions, and the rebuttal and cure process with its timeframes.
Document the reporting route — who receives QC results, at what frequency, and how results reach the Enterprises.
Record the required thresholds and the escalation path when a defect rate breaches them.
checklist.done: the QC procedure states the sampling method, defect taxonomy, gross/net rate definitions, rebuttal process, thresholds and reporting route.

checklist.step: Refresh the lender approval and monitoring procedures
actions: Update the Sections 600-601 procedure covering lender application, due diligence, financial and licensing checks, and the approval authority that signs off a new lender.

Document the ongoing monitoring regime: performance and delinquency review frequency, QC defect trends by lender, fraud indicators and the criteria for restricting, suspending or terminating a lender.
Document the master policy execution and amendment process and where executed policies are held.
Confirm the case management workflow steps match the written procedure step for step.
checklist.done: lender approval, ongoing monitoring, suspension criteria and master policy administration are documented and match the workflow.

checklist.step: Refresh the claims, rescission and servicing procedures
actions: Update the claims procedure to the master policy: notice of default reporting, claim filing requirements, documentation, decision timeframes and payment or curtailment calculation.
Document the rescission and denial process — investigation steps, evidence standard, notice content, servicer appeal rights and the authority level required to rescind.
Document the loss mitigation and workout handling agreed with servicers, including approval authorities and reporting.
Confirm the written decision timeframes match the SLAs configured in the claims platform and reconcile any difference.
checklist.done: claims, rescission and loss mitigation procedures are current and their timeframes reconcile to the claims platform SLAs.

checklist.step: Refresh the capital, reporting and records procedures
actions: Update the capital procedure to Sections 701 and 703 — sources and diversification of capital, Available Asset classification under the amended standard with its phase-in, and the Minimum Required Assets calculation.
Update the reporting procedure to the 800-series obligations: Exhibit B scorecard, Exhibit F loan-level dataset, Exhibit E certificate and Section 802 annual reports with their deadlines.
Update the records procedure with retention periods per record class and the production standard for an Enterprise request.
Have the Head of Capital Management and the Regulatory Reporting Manager confirm the written steps match what they actually run.
checklist.done: capital, reporting and records procedures are current and confirmed by the teams that execute them.

checklist.step: Run the annual review and approval cycle for each document
actions: Schedule each document's review on its own anniversary and issue the review task to the owner 90 days ahead.
Require the owner to record a substantive review outcome — reaffirmed unchanged, amended, or retired — with reasons, and reject a review that only bumps the date.
Route amended documents to the accountable approver and capture the dated electronic signature.
Publish the approved version with its effective date and retire the prior version into the superseded set.
checklist.done: every document has a dated, substantive annual review outcome and an approver signature, with the prior version retired.

checklist.step: Update documents within 30 days of a PMIERs or Enterprise change
actions: Log every FHFA or Enterprise publication that changes PMIERs requirements, with the publication date, the sections affected and the effective date.
Open a task against each affected document owner with a 30-calendar-day deadline from publication.
Record in the document change log which PMIERs change drove each edit, so a reviewer can trace requirement to text.
Escalate any document still unamended at day 25 to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: every logged PMIERs change has dated tasks against the affected documents and an amendment within 30 calendar days.

checklist.step: Assign training and capture attestations
actions: Assign each new or amended document to the roles that execute it — underwriters, QC reviewers, claims examiners, lender relationship staff, capital and reporting analysts.
Set a 30-day completion window from publication and require an attestation that the person has read and will apply the procedure.
Chase non-completions weekly and escalate anyone outstanding at day 30 to their manager.
Export the completion and attestation report per document and file it with the document record.
checklist.done: every amended document is assigned, completed and attested within 30 days by the roles that execute it, with an exported report on file.

checklist.step: Walk the written procedure against actual practice
actions: Select two PMIERs areas each quarter and sit with the performers while they process real work end to end.
Compare each written step to the observed step and note any step skipped, added, or performed by a different role than the document names.
Where practice is better than the document, amend the document; where practice is worse, correct the practice and raise an issue.
File the walkthrough note with the document record as the Section 302 'practices' evidence.
checklist.done: two areas per quarter have a dated walkthrough note comparing written steps to observed practice, with divergences resolved.

checklist.step: Control document access, versions and superseded copies
actions: Restrict edit rights to the named owner and the compliance librarian, leaving read-only access for everyone else.
Remove local and shared-drive copies of controlled documents and replace them with links to the library so only one current version can be found.
Confirm every superseded version is retained with its effective and retirement dates rather than deleted.
Run a quarterly report of documents with no owner, no approver or no review date and route each to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: edit rights are restricted, uncontrolled copies are removed, superseded versions are retained and metadata gaps are reported quarterly.

checklist.step: Report library health to the compliance governance forum
actions: Report documents in scope, reviewed on time, overdue by owner, amended for PMIERs changes and training completion rates.
Show the coverage matrix status with any PMIERs section still lacking a governing document.
Present open exceptions with owner and remediation date and repeat any item carried from the prior quarter.
Minute the forum's decisions and load actions to the tracker with owners and dates.
checklist.done: quarterly library health reporting is minuted with overdue reviews, coverage gaps and actions owned and dated.

checklist.step: Prepare the Enterprise production pack
actions: Assemble the standing pack: the coverage matrix, the current approved version of each Section 302 document, the change log and the training completion summary.
Have Regulatory Counsel clear the pack and record any privilege call on the index.
Test that the pack can be produced within 5 business days of an Enterprise request and record the retrieval test result.
Refresh the pack after every approval cycle so it is never assembled from scratch under deadline.
checklist.done: a counsel-cleared production pack exists, is refreshed each approval cycle, and its 5-business-day retrieval has been tested.

checklist.step: Archive superseded versions and approval evidence
actions: File every superseded document version with its effective date, retirement date, approver and change log under REG-050 / policies / year.
Apply the 7-year retention label and set superseded versions read-only.
Confirm the index allows retrieval of the version in force on any given past date, which is what an Enterprise reviewer will ask for.
Record the archive reference on the coverage matrix row for each document.
checklist.done: superseded versions are archived read-only under a 7-year label and the version in force on any past date is retrievable.

testing.step: Build the population of Section 302 documents
actions: Export every document in the controlled library with id, version, owner, approver, effective date, review date and PMIERs section mapping.
Independently list the PMIERs sections requiring written policies, procedures or practices from the regulation text.
Reconcile the two lists and treat any required area with no governing document, and any document not mapped to a section, as an immediate exception.
Sign the population as complete before sampling.
testing.done: a signed document population reconciled to an independently derived list of PMIERs written-procedure requirements exists.

testing.step: Reconcile the library to the systems and teams that execute it
actions: Ask each area head to list the procedures their team actually follows and compare that list to the library export.
Identify any working document, desk aid or spreadsheet in use that is not in the controlled library and treat it as a shadow procedure.
Confirm no controlled document has been superseded in practice by an uncontrolled instruction such as an email or chat message.
Log every shadow procedure with the area, the author and the risk it creates.
testing.done: the library reconciles to the procedures teams actually follow, with every shadow procedure identified and logged.

testing.step: Draw the document sample and record the method
actions: Take 100% of documents governing underwriting eligibility, property valuation, quality control, lender approval, claims and rescission, and the PMIERs capital calculation.
Draw 12 further documents at random from the remainder using a recorded, reproducible seed.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and selector name in the workpaper.
Publish the sample before testing begins.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all core PMIERs-area documents plus 12 random documents is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the currency and approval check on the sample
actions: For each sampled document, read the review date against the annual requirement and compute the days overdue where applicable.
Confirm the approver held the authority named in the governance standard and that the electronic signature is dated on or after the version date.
Confirm the review outcome was substantive — reaffirmed with reasons, amended, or retired — and reject a date-only refresh.
Log a document reviewed by its own author with no separate approver as a control failure.
testing.done: each sampled document has an in-date, substantively reviewed, properly approved current version or a logged exception.

testing.step: Trace each PMIERs change to the amended document text
actions: List every FHFA or Enterprise change logged in the period with its publication date and affected sections.
For each, open the affected document's change log and confirm an amendment references that change.
Recompute publication date plus 30 calendar days and compare it to the amendment's effective date.
Read the amended text and confirm it actually implements the change rather than citing it in the log alone.
testing.done: every logged PMIERs change traces to an amendment made within 30 calendar days whose text implements the change.

testing.step: Walk two documents against live practice
actions: Select the underwriting eligibility procedure and the claims rescission procedure and observe a performer processing real cases end to end.
Compare each written step to the observed step, noting any step skipped, added, or performed by a different role than the document names.
Test the written rule against the system's enforced rule — for example, the credit score floor configured in the underwriting platform versus the floor in the document.
Record every divergence as a fail regardless of which side is more conservative.
testing.done: two live walkthroughs are documented step by step, with every divergence between text, system and practice recorded as a fail.

testing.step: Verify training assignment and attestation coverage
actions: For each amended document in the sample, extract the assignment list and compare it to the current role roster for the executing team.
Confirm every assigned person completed and attested within 30 days of publication, and count the outstanding.
Spot-check five attestations against the version that was actually current at the attestation date.
Log any executing role omitted from the assignment as a coverage failure.
testing.done: assignments match the executing role roster and attestations are complete, timely and tied to the correct document version.

testing.step: Test version control and the retrieval of past versions
actions: Pick three past dates in the period and ask the librarian to retrieve the version of a sampled document in force on each date.
Confirm the retrieved version's effective and retirement dates bracket the requested date and that the superseded copy is intact.
Search the shared drives and collaboration spaces for uncontrolled copies of the sampled documents and count what is found.
Time the retrieval and compare it to the 5-business-day Enterprise production standard.
testing.done: point-in-time versions retrieve correctly within the production standard and any uncontrolled copies are counted and reported.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the document, the PMIERs section it governs and the nature of the failure.
Assign a root cause — no owner, overdue review, change not tracked, shadow procedure, training gap, practice divergence — and an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date inside 60 days for a documentation failure and inside 30 days for a practice divergence that affects loan eligibility or claims decisions.
Carry every open exception into the next annual library test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, root cause, owner, tiered remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the overdue-review rate, the coverage gap count and the practice divergence count against the stated zero thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references.
Have a reviewer who authored, owned or approved none of the sampled documents sign the workpaper with a segregation statement.
Report to the compliance governance forum and the Head of Compliance and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with the overdue rate, coverage gaps, divergence count and a stated conclusion is filed and reported.
