checklist.step: Open the certification cycle against the PMIERs requirement register
actions: Refresh the requirement register so every PMIERs section in force during the year has a row — governance, policies and procedures, underwriting, quality control, claims, lender approval, capital and reporting.
Assign each section to the accountable owner and issue the self-assessment task with a March 1 evidence deadline.
Confirm the current Exhibit E template and any certification instructions with both Enterprises in writing and attach the reply.
Publish the cycle plan with the February 1, March 1, March 20, April 1 and April 8 gates.
checklist.done: every PMIERs section has an assigned owner, an open self-assessment task and a confirmed current Exhibit E template.

checklist.step: Assess each requirement section and attach the evidence
actions: For each section, record the conclusion as compliant, compliant with observations, or not compliant, with a written basis rather than a tick.
Attach the specific evidence: the governing procedure version, the control test result, the audit report, the filing confirmation or the capital schedule for that section.
Reject any section conclusion whose evidence is an owner assertion, and return it for evidence.
Escalate any section not assessed by March 1 to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: every section carries a written conclusion supported by named, attached evidence, with unassessed sections escalated.

checklist.step: Prove the capital sufficiency position across all four quarter-ends
actions: Present Available Assets, Minimum Required Assets and the sufficiency ratio at each of the four quarter-ends, with the phase-in step applied at each date.
Confirm the ratio was at or above 100% at every measurement date, or document each date it was not, the shortfall amount and the remediation completed.
Tie the December 31 figures to the filed annual statement and to the Section 802 package delivered to the Enterprises.
Sign the capital attestation that feeds the Section 703 line of the certificate.
checklist.done: the sufficiency ratio at all four quarter-ends is evidenced and tied to the filed statement, with any shortfall and its remediation documented.

checklist.step: Prove the reporting obligations were met on time
actions: Export the filing calendar for the year showing every PMIERs submission, its due date, actual submission date and confirmation reference.
Confirm each quarterly Exhibit B and Exhibit F submission landed within 45 calendar days of its quarter-end and attach the confirmations.
List any late or restated submission with the days late, the cause and the self-report made to the Enterprises.
Attach the export to the reporting sections of the self-assessment.
checklist.done: the calendar export evidences every submission date against its deadline, with late items and their self-reports listed.

checklist.step: Build the failure log the certificate must disclose
actions: Sweep every source of known failure: internal audit high-rated findings, external audit deficiencies, QC threshold breaches, late submissions, sufficiency shortfalls and Enterprise-raised issues.
For each, record the PMIERs section, the date identified, the description, the remediation action, the owner and the status as at the certification date.
Confirm each status wording matches the underlying issue record exactly — remediated, in progress with a date, or open.
Have each failure owner confirm their entry in writing before the log is frozen on March 20.
checklist.done: a frozen failure log lists every known PMIERs failure with section, dates, remediation and an owner-confirmed status.

checklist.step: Reconcile the failure log to the issue and audit registers
actions: Extract every open and closed high-rated issue from the audit register and every open compliance exception from the tracker for the year.
Match each to a failure log entry, and investigate any register item with no corresponding entry.
Confirm no entry was dropped because it was remediated during the year — the certificate must identify failures and their status, not only unresolved ones.
Document the reconciliation and attach it to the certification file.
checklist.done: the failure log reconciles item by item to the audit and compliance registers with every difference explained in writing.

checklist.step: Draft the Exhibit E certificate on the current template
actions: Complete the Enterprise's Exhibit E template with the approved insurer's legal name, NAIC company code and the certification year ended December 31.
State the compliance certification exactly in the template's language, and attach the failure schedule identifying each failure and its status.
Prepare one certificate per Enterprise where the templates differ, and check every reference to a PMIERs section number against the current text.
Route the draft to the Head of Compliance and General Counsel for review by April 1.
checklist.done: a template-conformant draft certificate per Enterprise, with the failure schedule attached, is in review by April 1.

checklist.step: Brief the certifying officer before signature
actions: Build the briefing pack: the section-by-section assessment, the failure log, the capital sufficiency evidence at all four quarter-ends and the reporting timeliness export.
Walk the certifying officer through every section concluded as anything other than fully compliant and the wording used for it.
Confirm the officer holds the senior management authority the certificate requires and record that confirmation.
Answer any officer challenge with evidence before signature, and reopen the assessment rather than adjusting the wording.
checklist.done: the certifying officer has been briefed on every non-clean section with evidence, and their authority to sign is confirmed.

checklist.step: Capture the officer signature by April 8
actions: Read the certificate and the failure schedule in full and confirm each disclosed status matches what was reported to the Audit Committee.
Confirm no failure known to the officer is missing from the schedule before signing.
Sign both Enterprise certificates electronically with a signature date on or before April 8, leaving a week of delivery buffer.
Return the signed certificates to the Regulatory Reporting Manager the same day.
checklist.done: both certificates are signed by the authorised senior officer on or before April 8 with the failure schedule confirmed complete.

checklist.step: Submit the certificate to both Enterprises by April 15
actions: Transmit each signed certificate and its failure schedule through the agreed Approved Insurer channel to the named relationship manager, targeting April 10.
Capture the submission confirmation with its timestamp and request a written acknowledgement from each Enterprise.
Record the submission date, channel and confirmation reference on the filing calendar row for Exhibit E.
Escalate to the certifying officer the same business day if either Enterprise has not acknowledged within 3 business days.
checklist.done: both Enterprises acknowledge the signed certificate on or before April 15 with confirmations on the calendar row.

checklist.step: Submit the NAIC Market Conduct Annual Statement where applicable
actions: Determine which group entities and lines meet the MCAS participation thresholds for the data year in each state and document the determination for entities and lines that do not.
Load the MCAS data call in the NAIC MCAS application, populate the required schedules from the policy, claims and complaint systems, and clear every validation before submitting.
Submit by the published MCAS due date and save the submission confirmation and any state attestation.
Reconcile MCAS complaint counts to the internal complaint register and explain any difference in the workpaper.
checklist.done: MCAS participation is documented, validated data is submitted by the published deadline, and complaint counts reconcile to the internal register.

checklist.step: Track disclosed failures to remediation after certification
actions: Carry every failure disclosed as in progress or open into an active tracker item with the owner and the date certified to the Enterprises.
Report progress against those dates to the compliance governance forum each quarter until closed.
Notify both Enterprises where a remediation date certified in the schedule will be missed, before it is missed.
Require evidence of the operating fix, not an assertion, before closing any disclosed failure.
checklist.done: every disclosed failure is tracked to evidenced closure, with the Enterprises told before any certified date slips.

checklist.step: Correct the certificate if a failure emerges after signature
actions: Where a PMIERs failure covering the certified year is identified after April 15, assess whether the certificate as issued was inaccurate.
Have General Counsel clear a supplemental notice describing the failure, the period affected, the date identified and the remediation plan.
Sign and send the supplemental notice to both Enterprises promptly and record the send date against the certification file.
Brief the Audit Committee at its next meeting on the post-certification disclosure.
checklist.done: any post-certification failure is disclosed to both Enterprises in a counsel-cleared, officer-signed notice and reported to the Audit Committee.

checklist.step: Report the certification outcome to the Board
actions: Table the signed certificate, the failure schedule and the section-by-section assessment summary at the next Board or Audit Committee meeting after submission.
Minute the Board's acknowledgement of the certification and of every disclosed failure and its remediation date.
Load any Board-directed action into the tracker with an owner and a date.
File the minute extract with the certification record as governance evidence.
checklist.done: the Board has acknowledged the certification and each disclosed failure in the minutes, with directed actions loaded and owned.

checklist.step: Archive the certification record
actions: File the signed certificates, failure schedule, section assessments with evidence links, briefing pack, Enterprise confirmations and the Board minute extract under REG-050 / certification / year.
Apply the 7-year retention label and set the record read-only.
Confirm the index makes the record retrievable by certification year, Enterprise and PMIERs section.
Record the archive reference on the Exhibit E calendar row and close the cycle.
checklist.done: the complete certification record is archived read-only under a 7-year label and retrievable by year, Enterprise and section.

testing.step: Build the population of certified sections and disclosed failures
actions: Export every PMIERs requirement section assessed for the year with its conclusion, owner, assessment date and evidence links.
Independently list the PMIERs sections in force during the year from the regulation text and reconcile to the assessed set.
Export the failure schedule as certified and the underlying tracker and audit register items for the same period.
Sign the population as complete and treat any unassessed in-force section as an immediate exception.
testing.done: a signed population covering every in-force PMIERs section and the certified failure schedule exists.

testing.step: Reconcile the certified failure schedule to the source registers
actions: Match every high-rated audit finding, external audit deficiency, QC threshold breach, late submission and sufficiency shortfall in the year to a line on the certified schedule.
Investigate any register item absent from the schedule and determine whether it met the PMIERs definition of a failure.
Compare each certified status word to the issue record's status as at the certification date and flag any softening.
Treat an omitted known failure as a fail of the certification itself, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every register item is matched to the certified schedule or its exclusion is justified, and all status wording matches the source.

testing.step: Draw the section sample and record the method
actions: Take 100% of the sections carrying a disclosed failure and 100% of the capital and reporting sections (701, 703 and the 800 series).
Draw 12 further sections at random from the remaining assessed set using a recorded, reproducible seed.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and selector name in the workpaper.
Publish the sample before re-performance begins.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all failure-bearing, capital and reporting sections plus 12 random sections is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the compliance conclusion for each sampled section
actions: Read the PMIERs section text and form an independent view of what compliance requires before opening the assessment.
Open the attached evidence and judge whether it actually demonstrates compliance for the whole year, not a point in time.
Compare your conclusion to the recorded one and log every difference, including a right conclusion supported by the wrong evidence.
Treat a section certified compliant on an owner assertion alone as a fail.
testing.done: each sampled section has an independent conclusion tested against attached evidence covering the full year.

testing.step: Re-perform the capital sufficiency evidence at each quarter-end
actions: Recompute the sufficiency ratio at all four quarter-ends from the Available Asset and Exhibit A schedules for those dates.
Confirm the phase-in step used at each date matches the amendment glide path in force then.
Confirm any date below 100% appears in the certified failure schedule with its shortfall amount and remediation.
Escalate to the Chief Audit Executive the same day if a sub-100% quarter was certified as clean.
testing.done: the sufficiency ratio at all four quarter-ends is independently recomputed and agrees with what the certificate asserts.

testing.step: Trace the signature, authority and delivery
actions: Open the signature audit trail and read the signer identity, signature timestamp and the document version signed.
Confirm the signer holds the senior management authority the certificate requires, from the delegation of authority register or Board minutes.
Confirm the signed version is the one delivered to each Enterprise by comparing file hashes or the attached schedule contents.
Capture the signature trail and the delivery confirmations into the workpaper.
testing.done: the signature trail evidences an authorised senior officer signing the exact version that was delivered to both Enterprises.

testing.step: Recompute the certification deadline maths
actions: Confirm the certification covers the year ended December 31 and that the delivery date is on or before April 15.
Recompute the days between signature and delivery and between delivery and the deadline to quantify the buffer used.
Recompute the 45-calendar-day clocks on each quarter's Exhibit B and Exhibit F submissions relied on in the reporting sections.
Flag delivery on April 15 itself as a timeliness risk even where it passed.
testing.done: the April 15 delivery and every supporting 45-day clock are recomputed against actual dates with the buffer quantified.

testing.step: Test post-certification tracking of disclosed failures
actions: For each failure certified as in progress, open the tracker item and compare the certified remediation date to the actual closure date.
Confirm closure rests on evidence of the operating fix rather than an owner assertion.
Confirm the Enterprises were notified before any certified remediation date was missed, and read the notification.
Log any silently missed certified date as a reportable breach of the certification.
testing.done: every disclosed failure traces to evidenced closure or to a pre-emptive Enterprise notification of the slipped date.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the PMIERs section, the assertion tested and how the evidence fell short.
Assign a root cause — section unassessed, evidence absent, failure omitted, status softened, late delivery, unauthorised signer — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and decide whether a supplemental disclosure to the Enterprises is required, with General Counsel input.
Carry every open exception into the next certification cycle as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a documented supplemental-disclosure decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the section exception rate and the count of omitted or softened failures against the stated zero thresholds.
Write the conclusion on whether the certificate was supportable as signed, citing the workpaper references.
Have a reviewer who assessed no section and owned no disclosed failure sign the workpaper with a segregation statement.
Report to the Audit Committee and the certifying officer and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper stating whether the certificate was supportable, with exception rate and omissions, is filed and reported.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Underwriting Quality / Audit Manager owns the Sections 502-504 post-closing quality control programme — sample selection, review execution, gross and net defect rate measurement and reporting against the required thresholds; the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager owns the challenge and escalation of the results

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — PMIERs (Sept 27, 2018) Sections 502-504 (Post-Closing Review, Sampling, Defect Rates, QC Reporting) read with Section 402 property valuation and Sections 600-601 lender monitoring, re-verified at the start of each quarterly review cycle

In-scope processes.value: Quarterly post-closing quality control over insured mortgage loans — random and discretionary sample selection from the quarter's new insurance written, full re-underwriting review, defect classification, lender rebuttal and cure, gross and net defect rate calculation, threshold comparison and reporting to management, the Enterprises and lender monitoring

In-scope systems.value: Insured loan inventory and the original underwriting decision record used to draw the sample and re-underwrite each file; defect findings, rebuttals and cures tracked in the QC case workflow and rates published from the reporting warehouse

Compliance procedure documented.value: Post-Closing Quality Control Procedure — Section 503 sampling methodology and sample sizes, review scope per loan, defect taxonomy with severity levels, rebuttal and cure timeframes, gross and net defect rate formulas and the threshold escalation ladder

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Underwriting Officer and the Head of Compliance; re-approved annually and whenever an Enterprise changes the sampling methodology, the defect taxonomy or the reportable thresholds

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Quarterly cycle — sample drawn within 15 calendar days of quarter-end, reviews completed within 60 days of selection, lender rebuttal window 30 calendar days, net rates finalised and reported inside the 45-calendar-day Exhibit B submission window for the following quarter

Deadline reminders configured.value: QC workflow alerts at sample draw +30 and +50 days for open reviews, rebuttal receipt +20 and +28 days for open rebuttals, and an escalation to the Chief Underwriting Officer on any review still open at day 60

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Sample selection file with the seed and population, the completed review worksheet and re-underwriting evidence per loan, defect findings with severity, lender rebuttal and cure documentation, and the quarterly rate calculation — retained 7 years

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A gross or net defect rate above the required threshold, a sample drawn off methodology, a review closed without full re-underwriting, or a defect cured without evidence is logged with the quarter, the lender and the corrective action

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Chief Underwriting Officer signs off the corrective action plan for any lender or defect category breaching threshold, including delegation suspension decisions

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The quarter's new insurance written loan population from which the QC sample is drawn, every completed QC review file for the quarter, and the gross and net defect rate calculations reported to management and to the Enterprises

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Sample size and methodology must match Section 503 exactly — any deviation is a fail; recomputed gross or net defect rate differing from the reported rate by more than 0.5 percentage points is a fail; any rate above the required threshold without an approved corrective action plan is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is quarterly; the test runs each quarter within 20 business days of the rate being reported, with an annual methodology re-derivation against the current PMIERs Section 503 text

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Internal Auditor must sit outside Underwriting and the QC function and must not have underwritten or reviewed any sampled loan

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly QC verification workpaper (population reconciliation, sample re-draw, re-underwriting re-performance, rate recomputation, threshold analysis) in the compliance evidence repository under REG-050 / QC / quarter

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Sampling methodology with the quarter's seed and population, completed review files, defect and rebuttal records, and the gross/net rate calculation against thresholds — producible to an Enterprise QC reviewer within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Underwriting Quality / Audit Manager presents QC results to the Enterprises' quality control reviewers; a threshold breach is reported with the corrective action plan over the Chief Underwriting Officer's signature and tracked to closure

checklist.step: Re-derive the Section 503 sampling methodology for the quarter
actions: Read PMIERs Sections 502-504 and each Enterprise's current QC guidance and record the required random sample basis, minimum sample size, confidence and precision, and the discretionary sampling triggers.
Compare against the methodology used last quarter and log any change with its effective quarter.
Confirm the required reporting thresholds for gross and net defect rates and record them as the quarter's pass/fail lines.
Publish the frozen methodology for the quarter before the population is built.
checklist.done: the quarter's sampling basis, sample size, discretionary triggers and defect rate thresholds are re-derived from the PMIERs text and frozen.

checklist.step: Build the reviewable loan population for the quarter
actions: Extract all loans with insurance certificates effective in the quarter, with lender, channel (delegated versus non-delegated), loan amount, LTV, credit score, occupancy, property type and coverage percentage.
Reconcile the extract's loan count and insurance in force to the new insurance written reported in the quarterly statement and the Exhibit F dataset.
Remove nothing from the population without a documented reason approved by the Underwriting Quality / Audit Manager.
Publish the population with a record count, control total and an extraction timestamp.
checklist.done: the quarter's population is extracted, reconciled to new insurance written and Exhibit F, and published with control totals.

checklist.step: Draw the random and discretionary samples
actions: Draw the random sample to the frozen methodology using a recorded seed, and record the seed, population size, sample size and draw date so the sample can be re-drawn exactly.

Draw the discretionary sample against the defined triggers: high LTV with low credit score, new or newly delegated lenders, self-employed or limited-documentation income, high-value loans and early payment defaults.
Confirm the random sample is not contaminated by discretionary selections — the two must be tracked and rated separately.
Publish both sample lists with the selection basis on each loan and open a review case per loan in the QC workflow.
checklist.done: random and discretionary samples are drawn separately to the frozen methodology, with the seed recorded and a review case opened per loan.

checklist.step: Re-underwrite each sampled loan against the eligibility criteria
actions: Pull the full origination file for each sampled loan — application, income and asset documentation, credit report, appraisal, closing documents and the original underwriting decision.
Re-underwrite the loan from the documents without reading the original decision rationale first, testing eligibility, income and asset calculation, liabilities and DTI, and coverage percentage.
Recalculate qualifying income and DTI independently and compare to the figures relied on at origination, recording the variance.
Record the review outcome per loan as acceptable, defect with severity, or unable to conclude pending documents.
checklist.done: each sampled loan is independently re-underwritten from source documents with income and DTI recalculated and an outcome recorded.

checklist.step: Test the Section 402 property valuation on each sampled loan
actions: Confirm the valuation used was from an acceptable source and dated within the required window before the note date.
Review the appraisal for the required content — comparable selection, adjustments, condition rating and the appraiser's licence status — and check for value support.
Order or reference a valuation review or automated valuation comparison where the value appears unsupported, and record the variance percentage.
Raise a valuation defect where the value is unsupported or the appraisal fails the Section 402 requirements, at the severity the taxonomy prescribes.
checklist.done: every sampled loan has a documented valuation review against Section 402 with any unsupported value raised as a graded defect.

checklist.step: Classify each finding under the defect taxonomy
actions: Assign each finding a defect category — eligibility, income, assets, credit, collateral, documentation, data integrity, fraud indicator — and a severity level from the approved taxonomy.
Distinguish findings that would have changed the insurance decision from findings that would not, since only the former drive the reportable rate under the methodology.
Refer any suspected misrepresentation to the SIU Investigator the same day and mark the loan pending the fraud outcome.
Have a second reviewer concur on every severe defect before it is issued to the lender.
checklist.done: every finding carries a category, a severity, a decision-impact flag, a second-reviewer concurrence where severe and a fraud referral where indicated.

checklist.step: Issue findings to lenders and run the rebuttal window
actions: Issue each defect to the originating lender with the loan identifier, the requirement breached, the evidence relied on and the documents that would cure it.
Open the 30-calendar-day rebuttal window and record the issue date and the due date on the case.
Log every rebuttal with the documents supplied and route it to a reviewer who did not raise the original defect.
Close the rebuttal as upheld, cured or overturned with a written basis, and never let a rebuttal lapse into a silent cure.
checklist.done: every defect is issued with cure guidance, the 30-day window is tracked, and each rebuttal is independently concluded in writing.

checklist.step: Compute the gross and net defect rates
actions: Compute the gross defect rate as decision-impacting defects before rebuttal over the reviewed random sample, strictly to the frozen formula.
Compute the net defect rate after upheld rebuttals and evidenced cures, showing the reconciliation from gross to net loan by loan.
Compute the rates separately for the random and discretionary samples, and by lender, channel and defect category.
Version and lock the rate calculation with the quarter tag and the seed that produced the sample.
checklist.done: gross and net defect rates are computed to the frozen formulas with a loan-level gross-to-net reconciliation and lender and category cuts.

checklist.step: Compare rates to thresholds and open the escalation
actions: Compare the quarter's gross and net rates to the required PMIERs thresholds and to the prior four quarters' trend.
Where a threshold is breached, open an escalation the same week naming the driving defect categories and the lenders concentrated in them.
Where the trend deteriorates for two consecutive quarters without breaching, open a watch item rather than waiting for the breach.
Record the threshold comparison and the escalation decision in the quarterly QC report.
checklist.done: rates are compared to thresholds and trend, with an escalation on any breach and a watch item on any two-quarter deterioration.

checklist.step: Drive lender-level corrective action and delegation decisions
actions: Rank lenders by defect rate and volume and identify those exceeding the lender-level tolerance under the Sections 600-601 monitoring framework.
Issue a corrective action plan to each identified lender with the defect pattern, required remediation, retraining commitment and a re-review date.
Increase the discretionary sampling rate on those lenders for the next two quarters and record the increase on the methodology file.
Recommend restricting or suspending delegated underwriting authority where the pattern persists, and route the recommendation to the Chief Underwriting Officer.
checklist.done: every out-of-tolerance lender has a dated corrective action plan, increased sampling and a documented delegation recommendation.

checklist.step: Feed the QC results into the Enterprise reporting cycle
actions: Supply the locked gross and net rates and the review completion statistics to the Exhibit B scorecard build for the quarter.
Confirm the QC figures reported to the Enterprises equal the figures in the internal quarterly QC report, to the decimal place used.
Attach the sampling methodology note and the population reconciliation to the submission evidence so a reviewer can follow the rate to its population.
Submit inside the 45-calendar-day window and file the confirmation against the calendar row.
checklist.done: the reported QC figures match the internal report exactly and are submitted with methodology evidence inside the 45-day window.

checklist.step: Report QC results to underwriting governance
actions: Present the quarterly pack: sample sizes drawn versus required, reviews completed and open, gross and net rates against thresholds, top defect categories and worst-performing lenders.
Show the gross-to-net movement and question any large movement driven by cures accepted without documents.
Present open corrective action plans with owners and dates, repeating items carried from prior quarters.
Minute decisions and load actions to the tracker with owners and dates.
checklist.done: the quarterly QC pack is presented and minuted, with the gross-to-net movement challenged and actions owned and dated.

checklist.step: Close the loop from defects back into underwriting policy and training
actions: Review the top three defect categories each quarter and decide whether the cause is guideline ambiguity, system configuration or underwriter capability.
Direct a guideline or procedure amendment where the requirement is unclear, and route it into the Section 302 document review cycle.
Direct targeted training for the underwriters or lenders concentrated in the defect category, with a completion deadline.
Require the next quarter's QC report to show whether the defect category actually fell.
checklist.done: the top defect categories each have a decided cause, a directed guideline or training action and a measured next-quarter outcome.

checklist.step: Preserve the review files and rate calculation
actions: File the frozen methodology, the population extract with control totals, the sample list with its seed, every completed review worksheet, rebuttal records and the rate calculation under REG-050 / QC / quarter.
Apply the 7-year retention label and set the records read-only after the rate is reported.
Confirm the index makes files retrievable by loan identifier, lender, defect category and quarter.
Record the archive reference on the QC calendar row and close the quarter.
checklist.done: the quarter's complete QC record is archived read-only under a 7-year label and retrievable by loan, lender, category and quarter.

checklist.step: Reconcile QC outcomes to claims and early payment default experience
actions: Join the quarter's early payment defaults and rescinded or denied claims back to whether those loans were QC-reviewed and what the review concluded.
Identify loans that defaulted or were rescinded but passed QC clean, and re-read those review files to test whether the review missed the defect.
Report the QC hit rate — the share of subsequent defaults and rescissions that QC had already flagged — as a measure of review quality.
Feed any systematic miss back into the defect taxonomy and the review scope for the following quarter.
checklist.done: defaults and rescissions are reconciled to QC outcomes, misses are re-read, and the QC hit rate is reported and acted on.

testing.step: Rebuild the reviewable population independently
actions: Extract all loans with insurance certificates effective in the quarter directly from the policy and insurance-in-force records, without using the QC team's extract.
Reconcile the independent count and insurance in force to new insurance written in the quarterly statement and to the Exhibit F dataset.
Compare to the QC population and investigate every loan present in one and absent from the other, including documented removals.
Sign the population as complete before sampling.
testing.done: an independently rebuilt population reconciles to new insurance written and Exhibit F, with every difference to the QC population explained.

testing.step: Re-draw the sample from the recorded seed and methodology
actions: Read the frozen methodology and re-derive the required random sample size from PMIERs Section 503 rather than accepting the recorded size.
Re-run the selection using the recorded seed on the independently rebuilt population and compare the resulting loan list to the QC sample.
Confirm the discretionary sample was selected against the defined triggers and is tracked separately from the random sample.
Treat any difference in sample size, basis or contamination between the two samples as a fail.
testing.done: the sample is re-drawn from the recorded seed and matches the QC sample in size, basis and separation of random from discretionary.

testing.step: Select the review files to re-perform
actions: Take 100% of loans with a severe defect, 100% of rebuttals concluded as overturned or cured, and 100% of loans reviewed clean that later defaulted in the quarter.
Draw 25 further completed review files at random from the remaining sample using a recorded, reproducible seed.
Record the seed, population sizes, selection date and selector name in the workpaper.
Publish the selection to the Internal Auditor before re-performance begins.
testing.done: a reproducible selection covering severe defects, overturned rebuttals, clean-but-defaulted loans and 25 random files is documented.

testing.step: Re-underwrite the selected loans independently
actions: Open the origination file for each selected loan and re-underwrite it from the documents without reading the QC reviewer's conclusion.
Recalculate qualifying income, DTI and LTV independently and test eligibility against the guidelines in force at the note date, not today's.
Compare your conclusion to the QC conclusion and record every difference, including a defect QC found but graded at the wrong severity.
Capture the source documents relied on into the workpaper.
testing.done: each selected loan has an independent re-underwriting conclusion with income, DTI and LTV recalculated and differences recorded.

testing.step: Test the rebuttal and cure evidence
actions: For each overturned or cured defect, read the documents the lender supplied and judge whether they genuinely cure the requirement breached.
Confirm the rebuttal was concluded by someone other than the reviewer who raised the defect, from the case audit trail.
Confirm each rebuttal was concluded inside the 30-calendar-day window and that none lapsed into a silent cure.
Treat a cure accepted without the curing document as a fail that must be added back to the net defect rate.
testing.done: every cure is supported by the curing document, independently concluded inside 30 days, or added back to the net rate.

testing.step: Recompute the gross and net defect rates
actions: Recompute the gross defect rate from the re-performed conclusions using the frozen formula and the random sample only.
Recompute the net rate after only those rebuttals you accepted as evidenced, and rebuild the gross-to-net reconciliation loan by loan.
Compare both recomputed rates to the reported rates and quantify the difference in percentage points.
Treat a difference above 0.5 percentage points as a fail and escalate the same day.
testing.done: gross and net rates are independently recomputed with a loan-level reconciliation and the difference to reported rates quantified.

testing.step: Test the threshold comparison and escalation
actions: Confirm the thresholds used are the ones PMIERs and the Enterprises currently require, read from the source rather than the internal file.
Confirm every breach opened an escalation the same week, with a corrective action plan signed by the Chief Underwriting Officer.
Confirm any two-quarter deterioration without a breach opened a watch item.
Check whether the increased discretionary sampling committed for out-of-tolerance lenders was actually applied in the following quarter.
testing.done: thresholds are verified at source, every breach has a signed corrective plan, and committed sampling increases are evidenced as applied.

testing.step: Trace the reported figures to the Enterprise submission
actions: Compare the gross and net rates in the Exhibit B submission to the locked internal calculation at the same decimal precision.
Confirm the review completion statistics reported match the QC workflow counts for the quarter.
Confirm the submission landed within 45 calendar days of quarter-end from the Enterprise confirmation timestamp.
Capture the submission evidence and the internal calculation side by side in the workpaper.
testing.done: reported QC figures match the locked internal calculation exactly and the submission timestamp is inside the 45-day clock.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the quarter, the loan or lender, the rate impact in percentage points and the PMIERs section breached.
Assign a root cause — sample off methodology, review scope incomplete, severity misgraded, cure without evidence, wrong threshold, late submission — and an owner.
Set a remediation date before the next quarterly cycle and require a restatement to the Enterprises where the reported rate was wrong.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a documented restatement decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the re-performance exception rate and the percentage-point difference between recomputed and reported defect rates against the 0.5 point threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind it.
Have a reviewer outside Underwriting and the QC function, who reviewed none of the sampled loans, sign the workpaper with a segregation statement.
Report to the Audit Committee and the Chief Underwriting Officer and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with the exception rate, rate difference and a stated conclusion is filed and reported to the Audit Committee.
